label: Bark
text: Young trunks stay smooth for years. Old ones turn dark grayish brown, cut into broad ridges by deep furrows.

label: Needles
text: Three to six inches long, thin and soft, crowded toward the ends of the branches. Each stays two or three years, then drops in fall.

label: Pollen cones
text: Pollen cones grow in clusters at the branch tips in late spring. The young seed cones, yellow and in pairs, sit close by.

label: Cones
text: Slender brown cones, five to eight inches long, the scale tips beaded with white resin. Each takes two years to ripen.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray-brown to bronze on young trees, dotted with horizontal lenticels. It then splits into long, narrow plates whose edges curl away from the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Feathery, 5 to 8 inches long, divided once into 15 to 30 small oval leaflets, or twice, into four to seven pairs of side branches of leaflets. The leaflets are shiny dark green above and yellow-green beneath.

label: Thorns
text: Wild trees grow stiff, branched thorns on the trunk and lower limbs. As a tree ages it stops making them in the upper and outer crown, but they keep coming on the lower trunk and its sprouts. The trees planted on campus are thornless selections.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Pods
text: Flat, reddish-brown pods 12 to 18 inches long that twist into corkscrews and darken almost to black as they ripen. They hang on through the winter and are messy once they fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small, greenish-yellow flowers in narrow, hanging clusters two to three inches long, among the leaves in early summer. Easy to miss, but sweetly fragrant, and they last about two weeks.

label: Bark
text: Old trunks turn blocky or deeply furrowed toward the base. Where the bark is cut, the inner bark shows pinkish.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Seven to eleven lobes, each ending in a bristle. They open pinkish red in spring, turn a glossy dark green, and finish russet to bright red.

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers hang in catkins as the leaves open. The female flowers are tiny spikes where the new leaves meet the twig.

label: Acorns
text: Barrel-shaped, three-quarters of an inch to an inch long, in a shallow cup that covers a quarter of the nut or less.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Young bark curls back in small papery strips. On old trunks it changes completely: dark reddish brown to nearly black, in thick, irregular scales.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to three inches long, roughly triangular with a wedge-shaped base and doubly toothed edges, paler beneath. In a hard drought even old trees yellow and drop leaves early.

label: Catkins
text: The male catkins form at the twig tips in fall and wait through winter, opening in April or May. The female catkins come out with the leaves.

label: Seed catkins
text: Small upright cones packed with winged seeds. Once ripe and dry they shatter, scattering the seed.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Greenish gray and smooth on young trees, darkening and splitting lengthwise into tight, regular ridges with age.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, with five pointed lobes, a little broader than a sugar maple's, and dark green all summer.

label: Flowers
text: Rounded, upright clusters of small lime-yellow flowers open in April, before the leaves, in such numbers that it is one of the showiest trees of spring.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras ripening in October, each wing one to two inches long, the two spread almost in a straight line.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Older trunks turn dark gray-brown with blocky ridges. On young trees the peeling flakes show an orange inner bark.

label: Leaves
text: Three to seven inches long and widest beyond the middle, with shallow rounded lobes or coarse wavy teeth rather than deep lobes.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers hang in clusters of catkins; the female flowers are tiny spikes where the leaves meet the twig.

label: Acorns
text: About an inch long, half enclosed in a warty cup. When the ripe acorn drops, the cup often stays behind on its stalk.

label: Bark
text: Rough from early on, soon breaking into irregular plates, and deeply fissured on the lower trunk.

label: Needles
text: Half an inch to an inch and a quarter long, rigid and four-sided, with lines of pores on every face. They stand out all round the shoot and sweep forward along its top.

label: Pollen cones
text: On most trees the pollen cones come out rose red, on a few yellowish green, and shed their pollen in May or June.

label: Cones
text: Two to four inches long, crowded in the upper crown. Young cones stand upright, turn to hang within a month, ripen by August, and shed seed from September into winter.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown to dark gray, fissuring with age, on some trees deeply.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches across and broadly five-sided in outline, in pairs on long stalks, dark green all summer.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Small yellow flowers without petals hang on long, slender stalks, a week or two before the leaves; a tree in full bloom turns pale yellow all over. Trees seldom flower before about 22 years old.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras about an inch and a quarter long, the wings at a narrow angle, green until they ripen brown in October.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Smooth gray on young trees and branches. Old trunks turn dark gray and split lengthwise into scaly plates.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: About four inches long and as wide, with three to five lobes and irregular teeth. They unfold tinged red before deepening to dark green.

label: Flowers
text: One of the first trees to bloom, weeks before its own leaves. Some trees are all male, some all female, some both; the female flowers are the redder.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras an inch or two long that ripen in spring, not fall. Red maple sets a crop almost every year.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Grayish to reddish brown, in stringy fibers that form a network of ridges and shallow furrows.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Foliage
text: Tiny overlapping scales, about a twelfth of an inch, in soft, flat sprays at the ends of short, upturned branches.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Cones
text: About a third of an inch long, yellow ripening to light brown by September; open, they look like tiny roses. Only the middle two or three pairs of scales bear seed.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Winter color
text: Its foliage tends to discolor in winter, dulling from summer green; several garden forms were chosen for keeping their green.

label: Shape
text: Seventy to ninety feet tall but only ten to fifteen wide: dense and strictly columnar. Canker in the upper trunk often kills it before it is full grown.

label: Bark
text: Deeply furrowed, the trunk often swelling with large burls.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four and a half inches long, diamond-shaped to triangular, green on both sides, on stalks up to two inches. The thin, clear edge has shallow, rounded teeth, each tipped with a gland.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Catkins
text: Reddish male catkins two to three inches long with deep red anthers, hanging in early spring.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Dark and plated, furrowed between the plates, dark brown to nearly black.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Needles
text: Three to six inches long, two to a bundle, stiff and dark green, in heavy masses along the shoots.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pollen cones
text: Pollen cones cluster on the new shoots in spring; they are not showy.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Cones
text: Two to three inches long, egg-shaped and stalkless, alone or in twos and threes, glossy brown when they ripen in their second year. The scales are ridged across, some ending in a short prickle.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on young trees, developing shallow, dark fissures with age. Cut it and the inner bark is pinkish.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Glossy bright green above, paler below, with conspicuous tufts of brown hair where the veins meet. Every lobe ends in bristles.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins grow from buds set the year before and open as the leaves develop; the female flowers sit on short stalks where this year's leaves meet the twig.

label: Acorns
text: Small, about half an inch, nearly round and often faintly striped, in a thin saucer of a cup that covers only a quarter of the nut.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown and fairly smooth at first; from about thirty years old it forms irregular, lumpy ridges. Shoots sometimes sprout from the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to under three inches across, nearly round with a lopsided, heart-shaped base. Turn one over: pale bluish green beneath, with patches of rusty hair where the main veins meet.

label: Flowers
text: Five to eight flowers, sometimes many more, on a stalk joined to a narrow leafy bract. The clusters stand up above the leaves, which only one other linden's do.

label: Fruit
text: Small round nutlets about a quarter inch long, densely covered in brown hairs, with a thin, unribbed shell that breaks easily.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown and soon rough on young trees, growing paler with age until the lower trunk is gray-brown in small, irregular plates.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Needles
text: Half an inch to an inch long, four-sided and sharp-tipped, glossy dark green.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pollen cones
text: Small pinkish-red pollen cones cluster along the shoots. The young seed cones stand upright at the branch tips, reddish pink, then turn green and hang down once pollinated.

label: Cones
text: Cylindrical, purplish green while growing and light brown when ripe, hanging from the branch ends like ornaments.

label: Bark
text: Pale gray and dotted with lenticels when young. It soon scales finely to show yellow to reddish patches, and old trunks shed it in large, shaggy plates.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Simple and alternate along the twig, each edge lined with sharp, regular teeth.

label: Flowers
text: Small and easily missed, opening in spring.

label: Fruit
text: A tiny, hard drupe about an eighth of an inch across, its surface netted with low ridges: no wing, as an elm's seed has.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Light gray with shallow ridges and furrows on younger trunks. The trunk often branches low into several upright limbs.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Up to three inches wide, on stalks an inch and a half to three and a half inches long. On short, stout spur shoots they come in clusters of three to five; on long shoots, one at a time.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Pollen cones
text: Only male trees bear them: short-stalked, catkin-like clusters about an inch long, on the spur shoots.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Seeds
text: Not a true fruit but a seed in a fleshy coat, yellowish green and plum-like, an inch to an inch and a half long. Cooked, the kernels are sold as street food in Korea.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Brownish gray, staying fairly smooth until about forty years of age, when it begins to fissure.

label: Leaves
text: On most northern trees the underside looks green, with only sparse hairs; farther south many trees have gray-green or whitish felt beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Hanging clusters of up to forty yellow-white flowers open in June and last about two weeks. One study counted 66 kinds of insects pollinating linden flowers.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Round to egg-shaped nutlets, a fifth to two-fifths of an inch across, hanging from a leafy bract three to six inches long. Wildlife eat the seeds.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray when young. With age it splits into long, wide strips whose ends curl outward.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, deeply cut into five lobes, on long stalks that let them twist in the wind.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Dense clusters of petalless flowers, greenish yellow to pinkish red, open long before the leaves. Male and female flowers come in separate clusters, on the same tree or on different ones.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: The largest seeds of any native maple: paired samaras about two inches long, the wings spread wide.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Slate gray and smooth, with a few fissures in old age, on a short trunk that is often crooked.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to five inches long, pointed, doubly toothed. They open reddish purple, turn dark green, and finish yellow to orange-red.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins about an inch and a half long hang from short side shoots in April, green to brown with red on the scales; the small female catkins sit near the twig tips.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Light brown nutlets, each under a three-lobed leafy bract like a small umbrella, in dangling clusters that ripen in October. The bract is lopsided, its inner lobe tiny.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Dark gray, cut into deep furrows between rough, rope-like ridges that cross and join.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Six to twelve inches long, made of eleven to nineteen oval leaflets, each with smooth edges and a tiny point at the tip. Bluish green, with little fall color.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Pea flowers about three-quarters of an inch long, in hanging clusters that open after the leaves, in May or June. Bees do most of the pollinating.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Spines
text: On young stems a pair of stout spines, up to an inch long, flanks each bud.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Fibrous, reddish to gray-brown, in shallow vertical or interlacing ridges above a base fluted into sharp ridges.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Knees
text: Hollow, cone-shaped knees rise from the roots, crowded where soil meets deep water; their height tends to mark the usual flood level. Tests have mostly failed to show they bring air to the roots; they may instead brace the tree against floods.

label: Foliage
text: Soft, flat needles in two neat rows along slender side shoots. In late autumn the whole shoot drops, needles and all.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Cones
text: Small, round cones that grow and ripen in a single season and hang on the branches into winter.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Buds
text: Big winter buds, a quarter to three-quarters of an inch long, varnished with sticky resin.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Five to seven leaflets, usually seven, spread like fingers from one stalk; each is four to ten inches long, widest near the tip and doubly toothed. They hold late and turn yellow.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Upright clusters up to a foot high. Each white flower has a blotch at its base that starts yellow and turns red, with stamens longer than the petals.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: A spiny husk about two inches across, green ripening light brown in early fall, splitting to free one nut, sometimes two.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Look where branches meet the trunk for black, V-shaped marks. Twigs and young branches are dark reddish brown; the trunk turns fully white only once it has some girth.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, oval and pointed, with doubly toothed edges; dark green until they turn yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins form in late summer, often in threes, and wait through winter before opening between mid-April and early June.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Seed catkins
text: Slender hanging cylinders that fall apart when ripe. Birds pick at them so busily that some seed drops as early as July.

label: Bark
text: Flakes in fine scales of brown, gray and white, leaving a mottled trunk; the lower trunk of old trees turns rugged.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Four to nine inches wide and leathery, with three to five shallow, maple-like lobes and broad teeth; bright green above, paler beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Dense round heads on long stalks, opening with the leaves: the male heads green, the female a bright burgundy red.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Seed balls
text: Usually one to a stalk, about an inch across, packed with narrow seeds. Ripe by October, the ball holds on through winter, then breaks up in spring, each seed drifting off on its hairs.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown to almost black, deeply fissured with age, on a short trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, with three to seven pairs of rounded lobes, on a stalk so short the leaf seems to sit on the twig. At the base the blade curls into two small ear lobes. They stay green late, then go yellow and brown.

label: Catkins
text: Slender, yellowish-green male catkins 2 to 3 inches long hang with the new leaves in spring. The tiny female flowers sit on short spikes, three or four together.

label: Acorns
text: Egg-shaped, about an inch long, one to five together at the end of a stalk 1 to 4 inches long. The cup covers a quarter to a third of the nut. They ripen in one season.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray to brown, deeply furrowed between firm ridges. Even young twigs can grow corky ridges.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Four to ten inches long and widest near the tip, where one big wavy lobe can make up half the leaf; the lobes below are cut nearly to the midrib. Glossy dark green above, silvery green beneath.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins hang from this year's shoots shortly after the leaves appear; the female flowers are small spikes where leaves meet the twig. Pollen from another tree takes better than its own.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Acorns
text: Three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a half long, half buried in the cup. They ripen in a single year and often sprout soon after they fall, and a bur oak goes on bearing them to 400 years of age.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Smooth, glossy and reddish brown, striped with long horizontal lenticels: a trunk easily taken for a cherry's.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, broadly oval, in pairs; dark green above, grayish green and net-veined beneath. They drop in fall with little change of color.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Tiny creamy-white flowers, fragrant, packed into clusters six to twelve inches high.

label: Seed capsules
text: Dry, warty capsules about three-quarters of an inch long, green turning yellow, then brown, in enough numbers to notice in late summer.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark and thorns
text: Rough bark that grows slightly shaggy with age, on slender branches armed with thin, sharp thorns.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, triangular with a heart-shaped base, lobed toward the base and sharply toothed. They unfold reddish purple before turning glossy dark green.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch white flowers with pink anthers, in broad, flat clusters. It is the last of the common hawthorns to bloom, and the scent is unpleasant.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Glossy scarlet haws about a quarter inch across, each holding three to five small stones.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Polished reddish to chestnut brown, banded with prominent horizontal lenticels.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; NC State Extension

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, oval and drawn out to a long, slender point, sharply toothed, with a pair of glands on the stalk. They unfold purplish or bronze.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Single flowers an inch and a quarter to an inch and a half across, deep blush pink, two to six together on stalks an inch long; each petal is notched at the tip.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Egg-shaped, purple-black, under half an inch long.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, breaking into scaly ridges as the tree ages.

label: Leaves
text: In whorls of three, unequal even within one whorl, six inches to more than a foot long on stalks of four to six inches. Crushed, they have no smell.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: White bells striped orange and spotted purple inside, in upright clusters four to eight inches tall. It blooms earlier than the southern catalpa.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pods
text: Eight to twenty inches long and packed with papery winged seeds, released when the pods split.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown to grayish brown on mature trees, thick and scaly, broken by irregular fissures into ridges.

label: Needles
text: Half an inch long, glossy, flat, in two opposite rows, each on a slender stalk. Along the top of a branch a row of short needles lies upside down, showing its white side: a mark of this hemlock.

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny yellow bumps an eighth of an inch across, like miniature blackberries, grouped near the tips of the branches in spring.

label: Cones
text: Oval, about three-quarters of an inch long, hanging from the tips of the twigs. Green and closed when young, they turn brown and open their scales to let the seeds go.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on young stems. With age it turns reddish brown, very thick and corky, and develops broad ridges and deep furrows.

label: Needles
text: Flat, soft, three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a quarter, with blunt or rounded tips, set around the twig or nearly in two rows. Two pale bands of pores run beneath. They smell sweet when crushed.

label: Pollen cones
text: Male cones oblong, red to yellow; the young seed cones reddish, with long bracts. Both appear near the branch tips in spring.

label: Cones
text: Three to four inches long, hanging, light brown, with rounded scales. They ripen in one season, late in summer, releasing seeds with a yellow-brown wing.

label: Bark
text: Orange to red-brown and flaking in thin papery scales on the upper trunk and branches; reddish brown and furrowed lower down.

label: Needles
text: In pairs, an inch and a half to three and a half inches long, stiff, dark green to bluish green: about half the length of Austrian pine's.

label: Pollen cones
text: Dense clusters of small pollen cones, yellowish green to red, ring the base of each new shoot, or candle. The smaller, reddish-purple seed cones sit at the candle's tip.

label: Cones
text: Small, pointed, egg-shaped cones an inch and a half to two and a half inches long, with no prickles on the scales; they start out half an inch long.

label: Bark
text: Shallowly furrowed on young trees and more deeply on older ones, though few now live long enough to show it.

label: Leaves
text: Six to nine inches long, narrow, tapering about equally at both ends, dull green; yellow to yellow-brown in fall.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Pencil-thin spikes six to eight inches long, crowded with small white male flowers, in July; the female flowers sit near their base. The smell is musty.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Burs
text: A bur of many slender, branched spines around one to three nuts, smaller than European chestnuts but said to taste better.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Thick, dark brown to almost black, cut by deep furrows into a rough pattern of diamond-shaped ridges.

label: Leaves
text: Twelve to twenty-four inches long, with 15 to 23 finely toothed leaflets. They come out late in spring and fall early. Pull one off: the scar it leaves looks like a monkey's face.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-green male catkins 2½ to 5½ inches long hang from last year's twigs in April and May. The female flowers are short spikes of two to five at the tips of the new shoots.

label: Nuts
text: Round, alone or in pairs, in a thick yellow-green husk that never splits open and stains hands and clothes. Inside is a hard brown to black nut, ripe in October.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and dark when young; with age it breaks into long, narrow plates that separate into scales, the orange inner bark showing between them.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long and as wide, smooth-edged and heart-shaped, with about seven veins fanning from the base. Look for a small swelling on the leafstalk just under the blade. Yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch pea flowers, pink to purple, in tight clusters of around seven, open in April all along the twigs and branches.

label: Pods
text: Flat, oblong pods 2 to 4 inches long, each with about nine seeds. Green by summer, turning brown, they often hang on, a little untidy, into winter.

label: Bark
text: Light ashy gray, scaly, shallowly furrowed into flat, narrow plates or blocks that loosen and flake with age.

label: Leaves
text: Four to nine inches long, with five to nine rounded lobes and no bristles, the gaps between them varying from shallow to nearly the midrib. Whitish beneath. A purplish or reddish brown in late fall, and a few hang on into winter.

label: Catkins
text: In April, greenish-yellow male catkins 2 to 3½ inches long hang in clusters. The small greenish-red female flowers sit in the axils of the emerging leaves.

label: Acorns
text: Three-quarters of an inch to an inch long, oblong, set in a shallow, warty, light tan cup that covers a quarter to a third. Green, ripening light brown in the fall of their first year.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light gray-green on young trees. Older trunks turn grayish brown, with flat-topped ridges between pale furrows that interlace in diamonds.

label: Leaves
text: Five to six inches long, on a stalk of 2 to 4 inches, with four main lobes and a broad tip cut almost straight across, as if snipped. Bright green, paler beneath. Some go yellow and drop early in a drought.

label: Flowers
text: Cup-shaped and upright, with six green to yellow petals banded reddish orange near the base around an orange center. They open in late spring, after the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: An upright cone-like cluster of winged seeds, 2 to 3 inches long. In fall the samaras turn brown and drift away one by one through the winter.

label: Bark
text: Thin, smooth and gray on the oldest trunks as on the youngest.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, oval with a long point, glossy dark green above. Straight parallel veins run out to the edge, each ending in a coarse tooth with a little bristle.

label: Buds
text: Long, slender and sharp-pointed, about three-quarters of an inch, light brown and silky or smooth. In spring they unroll into soft, pleated new leaves.

label: Flowers and nuts
text: Male flowers hang in round, long-stalked clusters in spring; the females sit in short spikes. They become prickly husks three-quarters of an inch long, which split in fall to drop two or three shiny, three-sided nuts.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light to silvery gray, handsome in winter, becoming more ridged on old trunks.

label: Leaves
text: Up to four inches long, heart-shaped and pointed, with a lopsided base and toothed edge. Glossy green above and felted silvery white beneath. A pale yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Clusters of seven to ten creamy flowers hang from a long, strap-shaped bract in late June and July, fragrant and rich in nectar. It is usually the last linden to flower.

label: Fruit
text: Small oval nutlets, tan to gray and under half an inch, hanging beneath the downy bract in late summer.

label: Bark
text: Fibrous and reddish brown, deeply fissured on old trees. As the trunk matures it broadens at the base and develops deep, sometimes elaborate flutes.

label: Needles
text: Soft, flat, under an inch long, in near-opposite pairs along slender side shoots, giving a feathery, fern-like spray. Light green in spring, deep green in summer, red-bronze in fall.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small round pollen cones, about half an inch across, hang in long chains from the bare branches before the needles come out.

label: Cones
text: Barrel-shaped, up to an inch long, of 14 to 28 scales, hanging on long stalks. Dark brown when ripe.

label: Bark and twigs
text: Gray-brown, maturing into deep, irregular furrows. From their second year many twigs grow two to four corky wings along their length.

label: Leaves
text: Four to eight inches across, glossy and deep green, with five to seven pointed lobes like a star, on a long stalk. They grow one at a time along the twig, not in pairs as maple leaves do, and smell sweet when bruised.

label: Flowers
text: Yellow-green flowers in round clusters in April and May, the males crowded on an upright spike.

label: Gum balls
text: Hard, spiky balls an inch or more across, made of many beaked capsules. They ripen brown in fall, hang on through the winter and drop from December to April.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and reddish brown with lenticels on young trees, soon peeling in fine, thin scales. Mature trunks are grayish brown and rough, with loose, scaly strips free at the ends.

label: Leaves
text: Up to five inches long, oval and sharply double-toothed, birch-like, dark yellowish green, on a fuzzy stalk. A plain yellow in fall, and often early to drop.

label: Catkins
text: The male catkins form the summer before and spend the winter on the twig tips in clusters of three. In April they lengthen and hang, red-brown; the small light green female catkins stand up on the new shoots.

label: Fruit
text: Drooping clusters of papery, inflated sacs like hops, each wrapping a ribbed quarter-inch nutlet. They hang from summer into winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light gray when young, roughening with age, usually on several stems.

label: Leaves
text: Rounded to oval, 1½ to 3½ inches, smooth-edged, with clear parallel side veins and edges that curl under slightly. Blue-green in summer, yellow to red-purple in fall.

label: Smoke
text: The small yellow flowers are easily missed. The show comes after: their stalks lengthen and grow long pink hairs, making loose plumes 6 to 8 inches long that cloud the shrub all summer.

label: Fruit
text: A few small, dry, kidney-shaped fruits sit here and there among the feathery stalks of the plume.

label: Bark
text: Shallow ridges and furrows, often with a corky look.

label: Leaves
text: Small, two to four inches, with three to five rounded lobes and smooth edges, dull green above and downy beneath. Fall color, when it comes, is a late yellow.

label: Flowers
text: Small, green and inconspicuous, in upright clusters in spring.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras with wings spread out flat in a straight line, the seeds often downy.

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown, with shallow fissures and ridges as it ages. The inner bark is pinkish.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long and under two wide, broadly lance-shaped, smooth-edged or a little wavy, ending in a single bristle. Glossy above, paler beneath. Many hang on, brown, into winter.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-green male flowers hang in long, drooping catkins in spring. The female flowers are small spikes at the ends of the twigs.

label: Acorns
text: Round, half to three-quarters of an inch, a third covered by a thin, scaly cup.

label: Bark
text: Scaly, with dark brown ridges and reddish furrows, often on several stems.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, three to eight inches long, broad and spear-shaped, smooth above and downy beneath. Yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Ivory to white flowers with long, narrow petals in loose clusters 4 to 8 inches long, on last year's wood, in late spring. Male flowers have the longer petals and put on the bigger show.

label: Fruit
text: Clusters of olive-like fruits that ripen dark blue-black between July and September, food for birds.

label: Bark
text: Shiny bronze to silvery gold on young trees, peeling in thin, papery curls that run around the trunk. Old trunks lose the shine and break into red-brown, scaly plates.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to four inches long, pointed, doubly toothed, the base slightly heart-shaped. Dull dark green above, lighter beneath; a clear yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Male and female catkins grow separately on the same branch. The males form in late summer, singly or in twos and threes at the tips of long shoots, and open the next spring.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Seed catkins
text: Plump, upright and hairy, about an inch and a half long, packed with tiny two-winged nutlets that ripen in late summer and are shed as the catkin breaks apart.

label: Bark
text: Dark brown to dark gray, peeling with age, dotted with pale, upright lenticels. A scrape shows orange inner bark.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches, oval, finely toothed, with side veins that curve up toward the tip. Set in near-pairs or almost alternately, on a hairy stalk. They stay green late into fall.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny yellowish-green flowers, under a quarter inch, in clusters at the leaf bases, each with four spreading sepals. Male and female flowers are separate.

label: Fruit
text: Round, glossy black berries a quarter to half an inch across, each with two to four seeds, ripening in fall on female plants.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light brown to gray on young trees, with horizontal lenticels. It ridges and furrows with age, becoming blocky. Branches meet the trunk in tight, narrow forks.

label: Leaves
text: Glossy, leathery and dark green, broadly oval with a short point, edged with small rounded teeth and often wavy. They turn reddish purple to bronze-red late in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Dense, rounded clusters about three inches across of creamy white, five-petaled flowers, an inch or less wide, cover the tree in April and May.

label: Fruit
text: Small, hard, round fruits half an inch to an inch across, yellowish green turning brown, inedible, though birds eat them.

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth with raised lenticels on young wood, like a cherry's; older trunks flake in irregular plates.

label: Leaves
text: Oval and toothed, but varying a good deal in shape and size from one variety to the next. The veins stand out on the underside, which may be downy.

label: Flowers
text: Five-petaled, an inch to an inch and a half wide, white flushed pink, the pink fading as they open, in clusters of four to six. The central flower, the king bloom, opens first.

label: Fruit
text: Large, round and firm, often with a waxy skin, ripening from late summer into fall depending on the variety.

label: Stems
text: Young twigs zigzag and are downy; older stems are smooth. It usually grows as a clump of several stems.

label: Leaves
text: Broad, oval to wider toward the tip, with a lopsided base and a wavy, toothed edge. The leaf buds are fuzzy and stalked.

label: Flowers
text: Spidery yellow flowers, each with four crinkled, ribbon-like petals, cluster along the branches from October into December.

label: Seed capsules
text: Woody two-part capsules, green at first and maturing light brown, each holding two shiny black seeds. They sit on the twigs alongside the new flowers.

label: Bark
text: Rough and coarse, gray to gray-brown, with deep fissures between scaly ridges whose edges curl outward.

label: Leaves
text: Twice divided, in five to nine pairs of side branches, each lined with smooth-edged oval leaflets one to three inches long. Paler and hairy along the veins beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Greenish-white, star-like flowers in May and June. Trees are male or female: the males bear clusters about four inches long; the females, fragrant sprays up to a foot long.

label: Pods
text: Thick, flat, reddish to purplish-brown pods up to ten inches long and up to three wide, on female trees. They ripen in fall and hang through winter, holding four to seven hard seeds in sticky pulp.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, half an inch or more thick, with shallow furrows between corky ridges that interlace in diamonds. Old trunks may turn scaly.

label: Leaves
text: Six to twelve inches long, in opposite pairs, with five to nine smooth-edged leaflets on very short stalks. The underside is pale and silky-haired.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny flowers without petals in April and May. Male trees bear tight, light green to purple clusters; female trees, looser sprays of greenish flowers.

label: Fruit
text: Narrow samaras one to two inches long, each a single wing that runs partway down the seed, hanging in dense clusters on female trees. Green turning tan.

label: Bark
text: Thin, smooth and dark gray, wrinkled on old trunks like an elephant's hide.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, oval, with seven to nine pairs of veins and a wavy edge with no real teeth, fringed with silky hairs when young. American beech's leaf has sharp teeth.

label: Flowers
text: In April and May, the male flowers hang in round, greenish-yellow tassels on long stalks; the female flowers sit in small reddish-brown clusters on short stalks. A tree may be thirty or more before it flowers.

label: Nuts
text: A bristly husk about three-quarters of an inch long splits into four in fall, freeing triangular brown beechnuts.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light brown on young trees, later peeling in patches into a mottled jigsaw of tan, gray and brown.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, an inch and a half to four inches long, oval and pointed, pale beneath with tufts of hair where the veins meet. The veins curve toward the tip, as in all dogwoods.

label: Flowers
text: What look like petals are four pointed white bracts two to three inches long around a small knot of tiny flowers. They open in late spring, after the leaves, and can almost cover the tree.

label: Fruit
text: Round, pinkish-red fruits an inch or more across, hanging on stalks one and a half to two inches long in late summer. Yellowish-orange flesh inside.

label: Bark
text: Young bark is etched with fine horizontal lines; old trunks turn shaggy and scaly.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, round to heart-shaped, with veins fanning from the base and a scalloped edge. In near-pairs on short side shoots. They open reddish purple and turn blue-green, then yellow to apricot.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny and without petals, for a week or so in early spring, on separate trees: red on males, small and green on females. They are pollinated by wind.

label: Pods
text: Clusters of two to four small, narrow pods on female trees, ripening in fall and splitting through winter to release paper-thin winged seeds.

label: Stems
text: Slender gray stems with loose, faint stripes, many of them rising together from the base.

label: Leaves
text: Three to four inches long, widest above the middle, pointed, toothed toward the tip. Glossy green in summer, yellow to golden brown in fall. Among the last leaves out in spring.

label: Flowers
text: Narrow, upright spikes 2 to 6 inches long, packed with small white flowers, often several together at the branch tips, from June into August.

label: Seed capsules
text: The spikes turn into strings of tiny, downy, three-part capsules an eighth of an inch across, brown in fall and hanging on a year or more.

label: Bark
text: Light gray-brown and fairly smooth when young, later in rounded, interlocking ridges, much like an ash's.

label: Leaves
text: Compound, unusual for a maple: three to five leaflets, sometimes seven, each two to four inches, coarsely toothed or lobed, on a two- to three-inch stalk, in opposite pairs.

label: Flowers
text: Before the leaves, on separate trees: the males hang in tassels on long, hairy stalks, their anthers often red; the females hang in looser strings, each with a long, two-parted style.

label: Fruit
text: Samaras an inch to an inch and a half long, joined at a narrow angle and hanging in dense clusters. Greenish yellow, turning brown in fall and hanging on into winter.

label: Stems
text: Light gray-brown, with small raised lenticels and leaf scars; old stems shed in thin strips.

label: Leaves
text: Heart-shaped and pointed, smooth-edged, gray-green to blue-green, in opposite pairs.

label: Flowers
text: Cone-shaped clusters up to eight inches long, often in pairs at the branch tips, of small four-lobed tubular flowers. Lilac, purple, blue, pink or white, depending on the variety.

label: Seed capsules
text: Smooth, flattened, three-quarter-inch capsules in large clusters, green turning brown, splitting in two to release four seeds.

label: Bark
text: Flaking in strips and patches of gray, orange and reddish brown over smooth under-bark.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four and a half inches, oval and toothed, dark green above with small tufts of hair beneath. Fall color runs from yellow through red to purple.

label: Flowers
text: Single cup-shaped white flowers two and a half inches across, five petals around a boss of yellow stamens, from June into August.

label: Seed capsules
text: Hard, pointed, egg-shaped capsules about an inch long, green turning brown, that split open on the bare twigs.

label: Bark
text: Smooth, light gray and speckled with flat white lenticels on young trees; dark gray, rough and slightly scaly on old ones.

label: Leaves
text: Five to nine inches long, with nine to fifteen narrow leaflets toothed only from the middle up. Good fall color.

label: Flowers
text: Flat-topped heads up to six inches across of many small white flowers in late spring, with a heavy, unpleasant scent.

label: Fruit
text: Bright orange-red berries a third of an inch across, in heavy, drooping clusters from late summer.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and shiny on young trees, banded with lenticels. Scratch a twig and it smells of bitter almonds.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long and narrow, glossy dark green, the edge lined with fine teeth that curve inward. Look underneath for a line of yellow-brown hairs along the midrib. Yellow-orange in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Hanging spikes three to six inches long of many small, fragrant, five-petaled white flowers, in May as the leaves come out.

label: Fruit
text: Cherries three-eighths of an inch across, red ripening to purple-black, in drooping strings in late summer. Bitter off the tree.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, thick and spongy, cut into deep corky ridges on mature trees. Press a thumb into it: it gives.

label: Leaves
text: Ten to fifteen inches long, in opposite pairs, with five to eleven glossy leaflets, velvety beneath. Crushed, they smell of turpentine. Yellow to bronze in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small yellowish-green flowers in loose clusters in May and June, on separate male and female trees.

label: Fruit
text: Round drupes a quarter to half an inch across, bright green turning black in fall, in clusters that hang on through winter. They smell unpleasant when crushed.

label: Bark
text: Gray on young trees, striped by dark vertical fissures. Older bark is ridged and scaly, peeling to show reddish brown beneath.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, oval, pointed, finely toothed, dull dark green and downy beneath. They open with or just after the flowers, and turn yellow and drop early in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Bells half to three-quarters of an inch long, white or tinged pink, hanging in clusters of two to five from last year's twigs in late April and May.

label: Fruit
text: Dry, oblong fruits one to two inches long with four papery wings, green and then brown, each with a single hard seed. They hang on into winter.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray, brown or almost black, breaking into small, square, scaly blocks as the tree matures, like alligator hide.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to six inches, oval, smooth-edged, in opposite pairs, with six or seven pairs of veins that curve toward the tip. Pale beneath. Red to reddish purple in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Four white, petal-like bracts about two inches long, each notched at the tip, surround a knot of tiny green flowers. In winter, look for the round, flattened flower buds at the twig tips, shaped like biscuits.

label: Fruit
text: Glossy bright red, oval, half-inch fruits in tight clusters of three or four, from August to October. Bitter to people, but eaten by many birds.

label: Bark
text: Light gray and smooth on young trees; on old trunks still light gray, but pebbly.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to twelve inches long, with seven to nine broad, smooth-edged leaflets. Yellow to orange in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Hanging chains up to a foot long of fragrant, inch-long white pea flowers in late spring. Most trees flower heavily only every two or three years.

label: Pods
text: Flat pods two and a half to four inches long, yellow-brown, in hanging clusters in summer.

label: Bark
text: Grayish and mostly smooth, studded with corky warts and short ridges that build up with age. On some limbs it is smooth enough to pass for beech.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, oval to lance-shaped with a long point, like an elm's but lopsided at the base and toothed only from the middle to the tip. A plain yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish flowers on the new shoots, with or just after the leaves; this far north, in late May. Easily missed.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Fruit
text: Round, fleshy drupes on stalks half to three-quarters of an inch long, one to a stalk, ripening deep purple in September. Each holds one round seed.

label: Bark
text: Reddish to grayish brown, thin and fibrous, shredding in long vertical strips.

label: Foliage
text: Tiny scale leaves pressed tight to the twig in four rows, in flattened sprays that hang down.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small yellow pollen cones dot the tips of the sprays in spring.

label: Cones
text: Small and round, green at first and turning brown; they take two years to ripen.

label: Bark
text: Dark, shiny and tight, with horizontal lenticels, on young trees. With age it breaks into small, chip-like plates.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to six inches, oval with a heart-shaped base, edged with fine single teeth. Golden yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins three to four inches long, green tinged with red, hang from the twig tips in early spring.

label: Seed catkins
text: Upright, oblong, an inch to an inch and a half long. They ripen over the summer and break apart to release tiny two-winged nutlets.

label: Bark
text: The purple-brown outer bark peels back in papery curls that stay on the tree, showing rose-brown to cinnamon bark beneath.

label: Leaves
text: Three leaflets, the middle one on a short stalk, in opposite pairs; silvery and finely hairy beneath, on a downy stalk. Among the last maples to color, bright red and orange, and the leaves hang on late.

label: Flowers
text: Small yellow-green flowers hang among the new leaves in April and May.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras about an inch and a half long, with broad, spreading wings and unusually large, hard seeds.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light gray to light brown on young trees, with orange showing beneath. Old trunks turn thick and deeply furrowed, broken into irregular plates.

label: Needles
text: Half an inch to two inches long, blue-green when young and duller with age, pointed or notched at the tip. Crushed, they smell faintly of citrus.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small pollen cones hang in rows beneath the needles in spring, red before they open.

label: Cones
text: Cylindrical, up to five inches long, standing upright on the branch, green or brown with a purple bloom when young. They break apart on the tree to release winged seeds.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on young trees, raised in blisters full of fragrant resin. Old trunks turn brown-gray, rough and scaly.

label: Needles
text: About an inch long, flat, blunt or lightly notched, deep green above with two white bands beneath, pointing forward and up along the twig. Spruce needles, by contrast, are four-sided and sharp.

label: Pollen cones
text: Clusters of small pollen cones hang beneath last year's needles in spring, reddish before they shed.

label: Cones
text: Two and a half to four inches long, purple-gray, resinous, standing upright near the top of the tree. In early fall the scales drop with the seeds, leaving bare spikes on the branches for years.

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth for many years, becoming furrowed into coarse ridges on old trunks.

label: Leaves
text: Three to seven inches, slender-pointed and sometimes three-lobed toward the tip, coarsely double-toothed, with fourteen to twenty pairs of veins. The base is very lopsided, its rounded half often hiding the short stalk.

label: Flowers
text: Small reddish-green flowers in tight clusters on the bare twigs in early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Flat, papery, rounded samaras with the seed at the center, in crowded green clusters that ripen in late spring.

label: Bark
text: Red-brown and aromatic, cut into deep furrows between corky ridges.

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches, smooth-edged, paler or whitish beneath. Fall color is among the best of any tree: red, orange, yellow and purple.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-yellow flowers without petals, in two-inch clusters at the twig tips before the leaves, male and female on separate trees.

label: Fruit
text: Blue-black, egg-shaped drupes about half an inch long, each sitting in a little red cup on a red, inch-long stalk, on female trees.

label: Bark
text: Light gray, with deep V-shaped furrows between broad ridges that flake away in loose scales.

label: Leaves
text: Up to nine inches long, broadest above the middle, the edge lined with rounded teeth or small lobes. Shiny above, grayish and downy beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Slender yellow male catkins two to four inches long hang with the new leaves in April. The female flowers are short, reddish spikes.

label: Acorns
text: An inch to an inch and a half long, sitting directly on the twig, one to three together, a third to half covered by a scaly, hairy cup. Trees seldom bear before twenty.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, sometimes peeling, marked with prominent horizontal lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, oval and finely toothed, smooth and green, sometimes with two small glands at the base of the blade.

label: Flowers
text: White, five-petaled flowers on long stalks, three to five together, in late spring.

label: Fruit
text: Round, bright red cherries with a single stone, hanging on long stalks.

label: Leaves
text: Leathery, evergreen, one to four inches long, narrow and widest above the middle, with a finely scalloped edge. They crowd in rosettes at the branch tips, glossy dark green above and paler beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Quarter-inch, white, upside-down urns in drooping clusters three to six inches long at the branch tips in spring.

label: Seed capsules
text: Small, dry, round, quarter-inch capsules that split into five parts, ripen in late summer and hang on into winter.

label: Stems
text: Reddish brown on older stems, scaly and split into vertical fissures; thin and peeling on younger ones.

label: Bark
text: Furrowed between flat ridges on young trees. Old trunks turn gray-brown to nearly black, broken into hard, square blocks like alligator hide.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, oval to wider near the tip, smooth-edged and bluntly pointed, dark green above and paler beneath. Leaves on sprouts and young trees may carry a few coarse teeth.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny greenish-yellow flowers, an eighth of an inch across, in small clusters on long stalks in May and June. Trees are male or female.

label: Fruit
text: Oval drupes three-eighths to half an inch long, green ripening blue-black from late summer, clustered on stalks up to an inch and a half long. Only female trees bear them.

label: Bark
text: Grayish to orange-brown, with flat ridges and shallow vertical furrows; on very old trees, coarse and deeply furrowed in curving lines.

label: Leaves
text: Toothed, up to eight inches long, with an uneven base: unlobed, mitten-shaped or three-lobed, often all on one branch. Glossy and smooth above, which tells it from the rough-leaved red mulberry.

label: Catkins
text: Small yellow-green flowers in short, tight, drooping catkins in early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Sweet, blackberry-like clusters up to an inch long, ripening in June on female trees: white, pink, red or purple-black depending on the tree.

label: Bark
text: Thin and smooth, light gray to reddish brown, sometimes mottled.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, narrow, smooth-edged and shiny, laurel-like, clustered toward the branch tips. Turn one over: the underside is silvery white.

label: Flowers
text: Waxy, cup-shaped, creamy white, two to three inches across with nine to twelve petals, from late spring, and now and then until frost.

label: Fruit
text: A knobbly, cone-like cluster up to two inches long. In fall its pods split and bright red seeds dangle out on fine threads.

label: Stems
text: Slender, smooth, gray-brown stems dotted with pale lenticels, several from the base.

label: Leaves
text: Up to five inches long, oval to widest above the middle, smooth-edged, thick and light green.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny greenish-yellow flowers without petals, in little clusters all along the bare branches in March and April, male and female on separate shrubs; the male clusters are larger.

label: Fruit
text: Glossy scarlet, oval, half an inch long, spicy-scented, along the stems in August and September.

label: Stems
text: Arching canes, light brown, peeling in large thin sheets toward the base. Old stems carry shaggy masses of pale, loose bark through the winter.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches, oval with a long point, in opposite pairs, smooth-edged or with a few shallow teeth. Downy on both sides when new.

label: Flowers
text: Inch-long pink bells with a yellow throat, in pairs, in sprays about three inches across on downy stalks in late spring.

label: Fruit
text: Small, quarter-inch, egg-shaped capsules covered in bristly hairs, in loose clusters that hang on after the leaves fall.

label: Bark
text: Smooth on young stems, later gray-brown and sometimes shredding in strips.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Leaves
text: Narrow and lance-shaped, an inch and a half to four inches long, smooth-edged, covered with tiny silvery scales on both sides. They hang on late into fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small tubular flowers, silvery white to yellow and very fragrant, along the twigs from late spring into June.

label: Fruit
text: Olive-like, half an inch long, silvery at first, ripening yellow to red from August into October.

label: Bark
text: Pale gray, soon broken into small corky plates, and in time deeply fissured, on a single straight trunk.

label: Leaves
text: About five inches long, broad, toothed and glossy bright green, with hairs along the veins underneath. Yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Long yellow catkins hang in clusters from the bare twigs in March, one of the first signs of spring. The tiny female flowers are easily missed.

label: Nuts
text: Edible nuts in clusters of three to six, each wrapped in a husk of deeply cut, bristly, hairy lobes.

label: Bark
text: Rough, flaking and scaly, gray-brown, showing orange beneath where the scales come away.

label: Leaves
text: One to four inches, oval and pointed, smooth-edged and glossy green, in opposite pairs, with three to five veins each side curving toward the tip.

label: Flowers
text: Small yellow flowers in round clusters all along the bare twigs from late March into early April, before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Glossy, olive-shaped drupes half an inch to an inch long, coloring in midsummer and ready to eat once dark red.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and pale greenish brown on young stems, often faintly striped; older bark gray and slightly ridged.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, dark green above and pale, finely hairy beneath, the veins curving toward the tip. They grow one at a time along the twig but crowd into whorls at its end.

label: Flowers
text: Flat-topped clusters two to three and a half inches across of many quarter-inch creamy flowers, in late May and early June, after the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Small drupes, green, then white, then blue-black by midsummer, held on orange-red stalks. Each holds one large seed.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray-brown, on a trunk that is distinctly fluted, like flexed muscle. With age it splits into shallow furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, oval, doubly toothed, the straight parallel veins pressing in to give a quilted look. Bright yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: In spring before the leaves: yellow male catkins an inch and a half long, and green female catkins about three inches.

label: Fruit
text: Small, hard nutlets, each at the base of a folded, toothed, three-lobed bract, hanging in clusters on three-inch stalks in September and October.

label: Bark
text: Young stems range from green to polished reddish brown; older branches turn smooth and gray, often with fine pale stripes.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches across, palm-shaped, with five to nine lobes, most cut deeply. Green in summer on the species, red or purple on many garden forms; fall color yellow, bronze, purple or red.

label: Flowers
text: Small red to purple flowers hang in little clusters below the new leaves. Pretty up close, lost from a distance.

label: Fruit
text: Pairs of small samaras whose wings curve in toward each other in an arch, reddening as they ripen.

label: Bark
text: Smooth, charcoal gray to red-brown and dotted with resin blisters until the tree is very old, when it breaks into plates.

label: Needles
text: Flat, glossy dark green, up to an inch and a third long, with two white stripes beneath. Blunt or notched at the tip, not sharp. Those on top of the shoot are shorter and point forward.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small pollen cones cluster beneath the shoots in spring, shedding yellow pollen.

label: Cones
text: Cylindrical, up to six inches long, dark reddish brown, standing upright on the branches like candles. Their scales fall away to release winged seeds.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and brown-gray when young; on old stems gray-black and broken into small, flat-topped blocks.

label: Leaves
text: Three to four inches long, oval with a pointed tip and fine teeth, glossy, in opposite pairs, much like a plum's. Showy red to purple in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Flat clusters four to five inches across of small, strongly fragrant white flowers with long yellowish stamens, in May and June.

label: Fruit
text: Oval, a third of an inch long, green, yellow and pink in the same cluster before they turn blue-black in September and October. Each holds one flat stone.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, pointed and finely toothed, glossy dark green, the new growth yellow-green.

label: Flowers
text: Flat-topped clusters three to four inches across of quarter-inch creamy flowers, five-petaled, with long stamens.

label: Fruit
text: Half-inch fruits in pale green, yellow and pink, all in the same cluster, that slowly turn blue-black on red stalks.

label: Fall color
text: Orange to purplish red.

label: Stems
text: Young canes are often red; old stems have gray-brown, thinly furrowed bark.

label: Leaves
text: Oval and smooth-edged, reddish green in spring, blue-green in summer with paler undersides. Fall color is a fine mix of red, yellow, orange and purple.

label: Flowers
text: Small white or pink bells hanging in clusters in spring.

label: Berries
text: Round, blue to purple berries, each crowned with a little star where the flower was, ripening from green through pink in August.

label: Bark
text: Gray, in narrow flat ridges and shallow furrows, with reddish-brown inner bark showing in the cracks. The twigs are downy.

label: Leaves
text: Four to eight inches, broad, with a lopsided base, rough on top from tiny hairs. Turn one over: it is whitish and downy, with very prominent pale veins.

label: Flowers
text: Dense clusters of five to twenty greenish-red flowers on short stems, on the bare twigs in early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Flat, round, one-seeded samaras with the seed in the middle, ripening in spring.

label: Bark
text: Light gray-brown with irregular furrows, often streaked dark by weeping wetwood. Mature trunks are dark gray with shallow grooves.

label: Leaves
text: Small, one to three inches, oval to lance-shaped, only slightly lopsided at the base. Dark green above, light green beneath. Yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Light green to reddish flowers in tight clusters of two to five, on the bare twigs in early spring, before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Round papery samaras half an inch to an inch across, one seed in the middle, crowded along the twigs and scattered by the wind.

label: Bark
text: Gray, in flat ridges that braid and interlace up the trunk. Firm on most trees, flaking on old ones.

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches long, oval with a long, slightly curved point, rough to the touch, doubly toothed, and lopsided at the base. A plain yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-red flowers in drooping clusters of three or four, on the bare twigs early in spring.

label: Fruit
text: Wafer-like samaras, each tiny seed in a flat, oval, papery wing, in clusters on long stalks, ripe as the leaves reach full size.

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth on young trees, becoming shallowly fissured with age.

label: Leaves
text: About five inches long, heart-shaped with a pointed tip, medium to dark green above, light green and softly hairy beneath. Pale yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Drooping clusters three to four inches long of fragrant, pale yellow flowers with many stamens, hanging from a leafy bract in June.

label: Fruit
text: Small, gray, oval nutlets with raised ribs, ripening in late summer beneath the bract.

label: Bark
text: Red-brown and peeling in thin scales, on a trunk that grows short and enormously thick with age.

label: Needles
text: Flat, half an inch to an inch and a half long, set in two rows on either side of the shoot; shiny dark green above and yellowish green beneath, with no white bands.

label: Pollen cones
text: Male plants carry small pollen cones where the needles join the shoot, beneath it.

label: Seeds
text: On female plants, single seeds sit in a red, fleshy cup, the aril, open at the end. The seed inside, like the needles, is poisonous.

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown, cut by deep furrows between interlacing ridges; the furrows show reddish brown.

label: Leaves
text: Six to ten inches long, with 7 to 17 smooth-edged leaflets an inch or two long, pointed, green above and paler beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small, creamy white pea flowers, lightly fragrant, in loose sprays six to twelve inches long at the branch tips in July and August.

label: Pods
text: Hanging pods three to eight inches long, bright green and smooth, then yellow-brown, holding one to six seeds. They hang on into winter.

label: Stems
text: Yellowish gray to light gray-brown, warty with short raised lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, compound, usually of seven sharply toothed leaflets two to six inches long, set in pairs with one at the tip.

label: Flowers
text: Many quarter-inch, fragrant, creamy-white flowers in flat to rounded clusters four to ten inches across, in June.

label: Fruit
text: Quarter-inch purple-black berries, each with three to five small stones, in large drooping clusters in August and September.

label: Bark
text: Light orange-brown to dark brown or nearly black, with deep grooves and, on old trees, rough, shaggy scales.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long and only half to three-quarters of an inch wide, finely toothed, tapering to a long point. Medium to dark green on both sides.

label: Catkins
text: Male and female catkins up to two inches long, on separate trees, open as the leaves emerge, late March and April.

label: Seed capsules
text: Small reddish-brown capsules that split open to release hundreds of tiny seeds, each tufted with down that carries it on the wind.

label: Shape
text: Broad and rounded, the long slender branchlets hanging straight down, often to the ground, like a curtain.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown to gray-black, rough with irregular furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, very narrow, finely toothed and long-pointed, light green above and grayish green to whitish beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Slender, silvery-green to yellow catkins one to two inches long along the hanging shoots in April and May, males and females on separate trees.

label: Bark
text: Gray to yellowish brown, corky, and furrowed into ridges.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to four inches long and narrow, finely toothed, tapering. Medium to dark green above; silky white hairs make the underside white.

label: Catkins
text: In April and May, on separate trees: male catkins up to two inches long with yellow anthers, and greenish female catkins up to an inch and a half.

label: Seed capsules
text: By midsummer the female catkins are strings of small two-part capsules, splitting to release tiny seeds with silky hairs.

label: Stems
text: Young branches are covered in reddish-brown hairs, like the velvet on a stag's antlers. Older stems turn gray-brown and smooth, with lenticels, and finally scaly.

label: Leaves
text: Sixteen to twenty-four inches long, with 11 to 31 toothed, lance-shaped leaflets. Fall color is outstanding.

label: Flowers
text: Dense upright clusters four to eight inches long of tiny greenish-white to yellow flowers in late spring and early summer, male and female on separate plants.

label: Fruit
text: Upright, cone-shaped clusters of hairy drupes on female plants, bright red when ripe and darkening through the winter.

label: Bark
text: Nearly black on mature trunks, shallowly to moderately furrowed into irregular rectangular plates.

label: Leaves
text: Three to nine inches long, with five to seven pointed, bristle-tipped lobes. Leaves in sun are cut more deeply than those in shade. Glossy above, duller and paler beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Yellowish male catkins four to six inches long hang with the new, reddish leaves in May; the female flowers are short spikes of one to four.

label: Acorns
text: Rounded, half to three-quarters of an inch, half covered by a cap of loose scales that form a short fringe at the rim. Trees bear from about twenty, with good crops every two or three years.

label: Bark
text: Scaly on young trees; on mature ones gray to brownish gray, rough, in ridges broken by horizontal cracks into blocks.

label: Leaves
text: Leathery, three to eight inches long, with up to four rounded lobes a side; the upper pair is often much bigger than the rest, giving the leaf the outline of a cross.

label: Catkins
text: Drooping yellowish male catkins in April; the shorter female flowers sit near the twig tips.

label: Acorns
text: Egg-shaped, brown, half to three-quarters of an inch long, alone or in pairs on little or no stalk, a third covered by a cap of small, flat, pale scales.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and reddish brown when young, aging to gray or dark gray-brown with shallow ridges and furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Four to five inches long and about an inch wide, smooth-edged like a willow's, but tipped with a small bristle as red oaks are. Shiny light green above, paler beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Long, hanging yellowish-green male catkins in spring; the female flowers are short spikes.

label: Acorns
text: Rounded, about half an inch long, alone or in pairs, in a shallow, scaly, bowl-shaped cap banded brown and black.

label: Bark
text: Gray to black, with corky ridges and furrows that deepen with age.

label: Leaves
text: Four to seven and a half inches long, narrow and glossy, with straight parallel veins each ending in a bristle-tipped tooth. Golden brown to copper in fall, and often held into winter.

label: Catkins
text: Golden male catkins hang with the new leaves in May; the female flowers are on small spikes.

label: Acorns
text: About an inch long and oval, two-thirds sunk in a cup of long, spreading, curled-back scales like a bird's nest.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray with lenticels when young; with age it breaks into small, dark, checkered blocks or furrows.

label: Leaves
text: One to four inches, oval and finely toothed, glossy green on long stalks. Yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: White, five-petaled flowers in clusters in spring, their anthers dark red.

label: Fruit
text: Pears, varying a good deal in size, shape and color from tree to tree; teardrop-shaped is the most familiar.

label: Stems
text: Thin and smooth, gray-brown, on several stems.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to five inches, egg-shaped and finely toothed, tapering to a long slender tip, with a few hairs along the veins beneath. Withered leaves may hang on into winter.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant, half-inch white flowers crowded in cylindrical spikes about six inches long, in April and May.

label: Fruit
text: Pea-sized cherries in hanging clusters, red at first and black when ripe in August.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and silvery white to greenish. With age it turns chalky white, marked with black warty patches, and furrows near the base.

label: Leaves
text: About three inches, nearly round with a short point, glossy, finely toothed, on a flattened stalk that sets the blade fluttering at the least breeze. Golden yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Silvery, gray-green catkins hang from the bare twigs in April, before the leaves. Male and female catkins grow on separate clones.

label: Seed
text: The female catkins lengthen to about four inches of small capsules, which split to release four to ten tiny seeds each, wrapped in cottony hairs.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and greenish gray when young; old trunks ashy gray, roughened by long, deep, interlacing furrows and ridges.

label: Leaves
text: Triangular, three to six inches long, glossy, edged with coarse curved teeth, on a flattened stalk. Look for small glands where the blade meets the stalk.

label: Catkins
text: Catkins two to four and a half inches long in March and April, on separate trees: the males with red stamens, the females with yellow stigmas.

label: Seed
text: Female catkins lengthen to seven to ten inches of green, egg-shaped capsules that split in three or four to release masses of cottony seed.

label: Bark
text: Strongly ridged up and down the trunk, dark gray and deeply furrowed at the base.

label: Leaves
text: Broadly oval, four to seven inches long and three to four across, toothed, the base rounded or heart-shaped, on a round stalk. Green above and paler beneath.

label: Catkins
text: On separate trees in spring: the male catkins red-tipped, the female ones sparse and pale.

label: Seed
text: Clusters of oval green capsules along hanging catkins, turning brown and splitting to release small downy seeds.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and greenish gray on young trees, maturing dark gray-black with ridges and furrows at the base of the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: About five inches long, with three to five lobes and coarse teeth, a little like a maple's. Dark green above and white-woolly beneath, the stalk woolly too.

label: Catkins
text: In spring before the leaves, on separate trees: red male catkins over two inches long, small green female ones.

label: Seed
text: Hanging strings of capsules that split to release small downy seeds, easily carried on the wind.

label: Bark
text: Light brown outer bark flakes away in irregular pieces to show creamy olive bark beneath, mottling the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Large and maple-like, six to seven inches long and eight to ten wide, with three to five lobes, coarsely toothed or smooth-edged; paler beneath. Unlike a maple's, they grow one at a time along the twig.

label: Flowers
text: Small round heads in spring, the males yellowish and the females reddish, usually two to a stalk.

label: Fruit balls
text: Brown balls an inch to an inch and a half across, usually two to a stalk where sycamore's hang one at a time, packed with seeds. They hang on through the winter.

label: Bark
text: Dark and scaly on young trees; old trunks red-brown or yellow-brown in thick, flat plates between deep furrows. Tufts of needles often sprout straight from the trunk.

label: Needles
text: Three to a bundle, three to five inches long, stiff and twisted, dark yellow-green, with fine white lines of pores on all three faces.

label: Cones
text: Light brown, one to three inches long, in whorls of three to five, each scale tipped with a stiff, curved prickle. After shedding their seed they stay on the tree for years.

label: Pollen cones
text: Pollen cones cluster at the base of each new shoot in May, most of them on the lower branches; the seed cones form mostly higher up.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Bark
text: Smooth and dull gray on young trees. After about ten years it flakes away in patches of white, olive, light purple and silver, and turns milky white with great age.

label: Needles
text: Three to a bundle, two to four inches long, stiff, flat and sharp, medium to dark green, with finely toothed edges.

label: Pollen cones
text: Yellow, cylindrical pollen cones crowd the base of the new shoots in spring; the young seed cones are yellowish green.

label: Cones
text: Yellowish brown, egg-shaped, an inch and a half to two and a half inches long, single or paired on short stalks, each scale with a small triangular spine.

label: Bark
text: Thin, reddish to orange-brown, breaking into small scaly plates.

label: Needles
text: Flat, unusual for a spruce, half an inch to an inch long, glossy dark green above with two white bands on the silvery underside. They smell of citrus when crushed.

label: Pollen cones
text: Light red pollen cones among the needles in spring.

label: Cones
text: About an inch and a half long, hanging, violet-purple when young and ripening yellowish brown in October and November, with finely toothed scales.

label: Stems
text: The bark peels in long strips, showing several layers of reddish to light brown inner bark at once on older stems.

label: Leaves
text: Up to four inches long, round to oval with three to five lobes and toothed edges, dull green. A plain yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small white or pinkish five-petaled flowers in dense, rounded clusters one to two inches across, like a spirea's, from May into July.

label: Seed pods
text: Drooping clusters of small inflated pods, often reddish, from July to September.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray and thin, ridged and scaly between paler fissures on mature trees, becoming blocky with age. First-year shoots are often bright red.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, glossy and finely toothed, like a peach or laurel leaf; young ones have fine hairs along the edge.

label: Flowers
text: Small waxy white bells, all hanging from one side of slender, drooping sprays four to eight inches long, in June and July.

label: Seed capsules
text: Dry, five-part capsules a third to half an inch long on the same drooping sprays, ripening silver-gray in September and October and hanging on into winter.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown with a reddish tinge, in scaly ridges that peel and curl.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, heart-shaped and toothed, thin and dark green; unlobed or deeply lobed, often rough on top. White mulberry's are glossy.

label: Catkins
text: Greenish flowers in small drooping, catkin-like spikes in April and May, male and female usually on separate trees.

label: Fruit
text: Sweet, juicy, blackberry-like fruits, reddish ripening to dark purple, good to eat straight from the tree.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and silvery gray.

label: Leaves
text: Up to six inches long and one to two wide, narrow oblong to oval, smooth-edged and pointed, medium to dark green. They may turn yellow-brown before falling.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant, white, star-shaped flowers four to six inches across, each with about fifteen long, narrow tepals, opening one at a twig tip in March and April.

label: Fruit
text: Knobby, cone-like clusters of pods that turn red as they ripen in late summer.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, darkening with age and becoming scaly and fissured.

label: Needles
text: Five to a bundle, two to three inches long, straight and soft, blue-green with fine bluish-white lines.
