label: Cones
text: Two to three inches long at the shoot tips, greenish violet turning purplish brown. Unlike most pines' cones, they never open on the tree.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small, cylindrical and purple, at the tips of the shoots. Look too at the shoot: in its first year it is thick with orange down, which stays on into the second year, unlike limber pine's.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and mottled gray.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to four inches long, narrow and smooth-edged, dark green above and paler, hairy and finely netted beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant white stars three to four inches across, of twelve to eighteen strap-shaped tepals, from fuzzy tan buds half an inch long at the twig tips, in late winter or very early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Knobbly, cone-like fruits two to two and a half inches long that burst open in late summer to show orange seeds.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and brown to gray when young, breaking into close plates or scales with age.

label: Leaves
text: Five to ten inches long, thick, leathery and evergreen, glossy dark green above; underneath, pale green to gray-brown, often with a rusty felt.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant, creamy white, eight to twelve inches across, usually of six to twelve thick petals, opening one at a time in late spring and now and then all summer.

label: Fruit
text: Egg-shaped, cone-like clusters three to five inches long, rusty and downy, that split in September and October to let rose-red seeds hang out on slender threads.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray-brown, soft and furrowed, easily bruised by mowers.

label: Leaves
text: Six to ten inches long and three to six wide, oval with a point, the edges smooth and often wavy. Shiny yellow-green above, paler and hairy beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Greenish-yellow, tulip-like, two to four inches long and only slightly fragrant, at the twig tips from April to June. The leaves often hide them.

label: Fruit
text: Knobbly, cone-shaped, two to three inches long, red when young and brown when ripe, when red-coated seeds hang from it on slender threads.

label: Bark
text: Orange-brown, deeply furrowed into ridges that run straight, curve or fork.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to five inches long, glossy dark green, pointed and smooth-edged, on thin stalks one to two inches long that bleed milky sap when snapped.

label: Flowers
text: After the leaves, on separate trees: tiny male flowers in dangling clusters one to two inches long, and round green female heads three-quarters of an inch to an inch across.

label: Fruit
text: A wrinkled, yellow-green ball four to six inches across, like a large grapefruit. Inedible, and it oozes a milky latex when cut.

label: Stems
text: Gray-brown, deeply fissured and peeling in strips on old stems.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, oval with a long tapering tip, dark green above and lighter beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant, two-lipped, funnel-shaped flowers held upright in pairs along the stems from late April, turning from white to yellow as they age.

label: Fruit
text: Round, glossy dark red berries a quarter inch across, in pairs along the stems.

label: Bark
text: Scaly, furrowed and reddish brown on old trunks; smoother and gray on the branches.

label: Needles
text: Soft, bright green, about an inch long, in tufts on short spur shoots and singly along the new shoots. They turn yellow-amber in fall and drop.

label: Young cones
text: In spring the young seed cones stand up beside the new needle tufts, a crimson that early gardeners took for blossoms.

label: Cones
text: About an inch and a half long, upright, reddish brown, with scales covered in brown hairs.

label: Bark
text: Light gray-brown, with flat ridges between shallow reddish-brown furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Six to eighteen inches long, once or partly twice divided into seven to fifteen coarsely and irregularly toothed leaflets.

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch, bright yellow, star-shaped flowers with red centers, in loose sprays a foot or more long, in July. Falling, they carpet the ground gold.

label: Lanterns
text: Papery, three-sided pods an inch and a half to two inches long, like little paper lanterns, green turning yellow and then light brown, hanging on into winter.

label: Bark
text: Red-brown, peeling in long, narrow, fibrous strips that often leave ashy gray patches.

label: Foliage
text: Tiny scales a sixteenth of an inch long, in opposite pairs or threes, pressed along the twig in four rows, dark blue-green and shiny. Each has a small gland. Often brownish green in winter.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small yellow to orange-brown pollen cones at the branch tips of male trees in late winter.

label: Cones
text: Round, berry-like, a quarter inch across, blue under a white waxy frost, abundant on female trees. They ripen in their first fall and hang on through winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and olive-brown when young, turning light silvery gray with flat ridges in a diamond pattern.

label: Leaves
text: Twelve to eighteen inches long, with five to eleven broad, mostly smooth-edged leaflets, the one at the tip the largest. Black walnut's leaves have many more, toothed leaflets.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins up to six inches long hang as the leaves open in May and June; the female flowers sit in clusters of three to nine.

label: Nuts
text: Round, in a smooth green husk that turns brown and splits in fall. The nut, up to two inches long, has a thin, wrinkled shell.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray with pale lenticels when young. With age it forms narrow, flat-topped, pale ridges in a diamond pattern, between dark gray to black furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Ten to twenty inches long, with 11 to 19 leaflets including one at the tip, crowded toward the ends of the branches so they seem whorled.

label: Catkins
text: Slender yellow-green male catkins two and a half to five and a half inches long; the female flowers are short spikes at the branch tips.

label: Nuts
text: Oblong and pointed, an inch and a half to over two inches long, in a green husk with two to four ridges and short sticky hairs, ripening in September and October.

label: Stems
text: Gray to blackish, smooth, with knobby lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to four inches long, oval with a point, toothed but not spiny, hairy along the veins beneath. They drop in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-white flowers tucked in the leaf axils in late spring, on separate male and female plants.

label: Berries
text: Quarter-inch, bright red berries crowded along the stems of female plants from late summer, lasting on the bare branches into winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light gray to almost white, often warty or splotched with red and tan lichens.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, thick and leathery, evergreen, with spiny teeth along the edge and a spine at the tip.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-white flowers from April to June, on separate trees: the males in clusters of three to twelve, the females alone or in twos and threes.

label: Berries
text: Bright red, sometimes orange, on female trees from September, lasting into February.

label: Stems
text: Smooth and gray, many stems together.

label: Leaves
text: Evergreen, up to an inch and a half long, flat and glossy dark green, smooth-edged except for a few small teeth near the tip. No spines.

label: Flowers
text: Small and easily missed, in May and June, on separate male and female plants: the males in little clusters, the females in clusters or alone.

label: Berries
text: Pea-sized, jet-black and glossy, on female plants, ripening in September and lasting into November.

label: Stems
text: Smooth, gray to gray-brown.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, broad and rounded with a short point, lopsided at the base and toothed on the upper half, with five to eight pairs of veins. Pale and downy beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Four long, narrow, twisted petals like ribbons, yellow to red depending on the variety, on the bare branches from late January into March.

label: Seed capsules
text: Fuzzy capsules that split open in four, browning as they ripen.

label: Bark
text: Gray to gray-brown, with furrows between short, irregular ridges, often scaly.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, of five to eleven leaflets, usually seven to nine, two to five inches long, toothed and short-stalked, with a few hairs beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small clusters of tiny flowers in spring, dark purple, on the bare twigs before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Clusters of winged samaras an inch to an inch and a half long and a quarter to half an inch wide.

label: Bark
text: Light gray to yellow-brown and corky, deeply furrowed between short, pointed ridges that join in a tight net of diamonds.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to twelve inches long, in opposite pairs, usually of seven leaflets three to five inches long, smooth-edged or nearly so, dark green above and whitish beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Tight clusters of tiny purplish flowers without petals, on separate male and female trees, on the bare twigs in April and May before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Drooping clusters six to eight inches long of flat, single-winged samaras up to two inches, shaped like canoe paddles. They ripen in fall and may hang on all winter.

label: Winged twigs
text: Green twigs lined with flat, corky wings. The bark of large old stems is gray or brownish gray and slightly furrowed.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, oval, finely toothed, in pairs or nearly so. Medium to dark green, turning brilliant red in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small, four-petaled, yellow-green flowers in threes in the leaf axils, easily overlooked.

label: Fruit
text: Half-inch red capsules that split in fall to show seeds wrapped in a fleshy orange-red coat, eaten by birds.

label: Bark
text: Thick, dark gray, broken by furrows into small square blocks like a checkerboard. One of the easiest trees to name in winter.

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, broadly oval and pointed, smooth-edged, glossy above and paler beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small, fragrant, white to greenish-yellow bells in late spring, usually on separate trees: male flowers in twos and threes, female ones alone.

label: Fruit
text: Round, an inch to an inch and a half, yellowish to pale orange with a waxy bloom, the green sepals still at the base. On female trees from September to December.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown, peeling in long, showy strips.

label: Needles
text: Three-quarters of an inch long, awl-shaped and four-angled, curving in with a slight twist, spiraling around the shoot. They stay four or five years and may bronze in winter.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small, oblong, scaly pollen cones in clusters near the branch tips.

label: Cones
text: Small, round and brown, like little rosettes bristling with points, at the tips of the shoots, alone or in groups.

label: Bark
text: Thin and gray, breaking into narrow scales as the tree ages; on mature trunks it flakes away to show orange inner bark.

label: Leaves
text: Up to three and a half inches long, glossy dark green, shallowly lobed on the upper half and toothed.

label: Flowers
text: Small five-petaled white flowers in clusters about two inches across, smelling unpleasant to us and attractive to the midges that pollinate them.

label: Fruit
text: Small red haws that ripen in September and usually hang on well into winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth, thin and gray, fissuring with age; on old stems it breaks into thin, narrow scales.

label: Leaves
text: Glossy dark green, wedge-shaped and widest toward the tip, where they are toothed. Orange to scarlet to purple in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch white flowers in flat clusters two to three inches across in April and May. Pleasant at first, the scent soon turns fishy, which draws the midges that pollinate them.

label: Haws and thorns
text: Small, deep red haws, each holding one to five hard stones. The long, straight thorns are seldom far away.

label: Stems
text: Smooth brown bark with pale lenticels, on stems that zigzag from bud to bud.

label: Leaves
text: Rounded, with a heart-shaped base and doubly toothed edge, softly hairy on both sides.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-brown male catkins hang on the bare stems all winter and turn yellow as they shed pollen at its end. The female flowers show only a tuft of red styles.

label: Nuts
text: Round nuts about an inch across, one to five together, each in a short, leafy husk, released when they ripen in late summer.

label: Stems
text: Smooth and bright red, most striking in winter when the leaves are off.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, oval to lance-shaped, smooth-edged, in opposite pairs, the veins curving toward the tip as in all dogwoods. Orange to red to purple in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small dull white flowers in flat-topped clusters in early summer.

label: Fruit
text: White berries with a blue tinge, quickly taken by birds.

label: Stems
text: Gray to grayish brown on older stems, dotted with many small lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Two to three and a half inches long, narrow, in opposite pairs, dark green above and pale to nearly white beneath, the veins curving toward the tip.

label: Flowers
text: Quarter-inch, four-petaled creamy flowers, stamens as long as the petals, in rounded clusters at the ends of the branches.

label: Fruit
text: Quarter-inch white berries, each with one or two stones, on stalks that turn red in fall and early winter.

label: Bark
text: Gray to brown, peeling with age in small, irregular plates that leave patches of tan and orange.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, smooth-edged, in opposite pairs, dull green above and lighter beneath, often with tufts of reddish-brown hairs where the veins meet.

label: Flowers
text: Clusters of short-stalked yellow flowers, each cluster with four drooping bracts, on the bare stems in late winter and early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Red to purplish-red, oval, about a quarter inch long, in fall. Edible but very astringent.

label: Stems
text: Gray and somewhat peeling, developing furrows with age.

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches long, oval and pointed, smooth-edged, glossy bright green, in pairs or threes around the stem.

label: Flowers
text: Round heads an inch and a half across, packed with tiny fragrant creamy tubes whose long styles stick out like pins in a cushion, from June to August.

label: Seed balls
text: The heads harden into reddish-brown balls of tiny nutlets in August and September, usually hanging on through the winter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray between raised, corky warts.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, narrow and pointed, mostly without teeth, lopsided at the base. A plain yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish flowers in April and May with the new leaves, the male ones in clusters and the female ones single.

label: Fruit
text: Small drupes on long stalks, orange-red ripening deep purple from August to October, sweet and thin-fleshed around one round seed.

label: Bark
text: Light gray-brown and scaly, in thin plates rather than the ridges of northern catalpa.

label: Leaves
text: About ten inches long and six wide, heart-shaped and slightly downy, in pairs or threes. Crushed, they smell unpleasant; northern catalpa's do not.

label: Flowers
text: Frilled white bells in sprays six to twelve inches long, marked inside with two rows of yellow spots and many purple ones; a little later and more purple-spotted than northern catalpa's.

label: Pods
text: Long, narrow pods up to fifteen inches, dark brown in fall, splitting lengthwise to release seeds from October.

label: Bark
text: Tight and gray, in smooth, rounded, interlacing ridges with shallow furrows, on young and old trees alike.

label: Leaves
text: Nine to twenty inches long, dark yellow-green, with five to seven toothed leaflets three to six inches long.

label: Catkins
text: Greenish-yellow male catkins up to six inches long hang with the new leaves; the female flowers are short spikes with feathery reddish stigmas.

label: Nuts
text: Husks an inch and a half to three inches across, green turning yellow and then brown, splitting into four in October around one thick-shelled nut.

label: Bark
text: Scaly on young trees. With age it separates into narrow, flat plates one to three feet long that curve away from the trunk at both ends.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to fourteen inches long, usually of five broad, pointed, finely toothed leaflets three to seven inches long, the one at the tip the largest.

label: Catkins
text: Greenish-yellow male catkins three to five inches long hang in May; the female flowers are short spikes.

label: Nuts
text: A round husk an inch and a half to two inches across, green turning deep brown, that splits in four to free a light tan, flattened nut with sweet meat.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, in narrow, scaly ridges broken into rectangles.

label: Leaves
text: With 9 to 17 lance-shaped, toothed leaflets, often curved like a sickle. Black walnut has more and shorter leaflets.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-green male catkins about four inches long in April and May; the female flowers are shorter spikes.

label: Nuts
text: Oval pecans one to three inches long, tan to brown with dark streaks, in a husk that dries from green to brown and splits into four in fall.

label: Bark
text: Smooth with shallow cracks on young trees; with age, flat, sharp-edged ridges that cross in diamonds and X's.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to twelve inches long, usually of five toothed, lance-shaped leaflets three to six inches long, the ones at the tip largest. Smooth or nearly so beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow-green male catkins two to four inches long in April and May; the female flowers are very small.

label: Nuts
text: A thin, often pear-shaped husk about an inch long, green turning brown, that splits in fall to release a tan, slightly flattened nut.

label: Bark
text: Granite gray, faintly tinged yellow, smoother than most hickories'. Smooth at first, it breaks with age into a flat network of narrow, plate-like scales.

label: Leaves
text: Six to ten inches long, with five to nine long, narrow, toothed leaflets, dark yellow-green above and lighter beneath, a little downy on the veins.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins three to four inches long hang from last year's shoots or the base of the new growth in spring; the female flowers are short spikes at the shoot tips.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Nuts
text: Round, about an inch, in a thin husk with four winged seams from the tip to about the middle. The kernel is very bitter. Trees seldom bear before thirty.

label: Spines
text: Brown, zigzag twigs with a single sharp spine at each node, a tuft of leaves growing from its base.

label: Leaves
text: Small, half an inch to an inch and a quarter, smooth-edged and narrowed at the base, in tufts at the spines. Bright red to orange in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Pale yellow cups a third to half an inch across, hanging in twos to fives under the leaves in April and May, often hidden.

label: Berries
text: Glossy, bright red, oblong berries a third of an inch or more long, hanging along the stems from fall into winter.

label: Bark
text: Thin, smooth and brown, splotched with warty lenticels; fissured and scaly with age.

label: Leaves
text: Six to twelve inches long, widest toward the tip, hanging limply in two rows from the stem. Pale beneath. Crushed, they smell like green pepper.

label: Flowers
text: Purplish-brown to burgundy, an inch to an inch and a half across, with six petals, in spring. They smell faintly foul, to draw the flies that pollinate them.

label: Fruit
text: Green, oblong, with a whitish bloom, ripening from August to October to soft, sweet, custard-like flesh that tastes of banana.

label: Stems
text: Gray-brown, many from the base, the plant spreading by suckers.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches, oval, glossy dark green and finely toothed. Wine red in fall, varying from plant to plant.

label: Flowers
text: Third-inch, five-petaled, off-white flowers with pink anthers, five or six together, in May and June.

label: Fruit
text: Shiny blackish-purple berries half an inch across, ripening in August and September.

label: Prickly stems
text: Stout, sparse, mostly unbranched stems like clubs, ringed with leaf scars and armed, like the leaf stalks, with sharp spines.

label: Leaves
text: Enormous, two to five feet long and two to four wide, divided twice or three times into toothed leaflets two to four inches long, all crowded near the top of the stem.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny, five-petaled white flowers in huge branched sprays up to two feet long at the top of the plant, in summer.

label: Fruit
text: Round, fleshy purple-black drupes in compact clusters on red stalks, ripening from late July into October, quickly eaten by birds.

label: Prickly stems
text: Stout gray stems with sharp thorns.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four feet long, divided two or three times into as many as eighty leaflets three to five and a half inches long, whose main veins run right to the tip, unlike the native devil's walking stick's.

label: Flowers
text: White to cream sprays a foot to a foot and a half across, wider than tall, from late July into August.

label: Fruit
text: Round, purple to black drupes in clusters, ripening into fall.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and slate-gray with paler or darker vertical stripes; on mature trees it splits and roughens.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, oval, finely toothed, abruptly pointed. They open bronze-purple and nearly hairless, then turn glossy green; clear yellow to red in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small white flowers with long, narrow petals, in loose clusters about four inches long, as or just before the leaves open.

label: Fruit
text: Sweet, blueberry-like fruits on long stalks, red ripening to purple in June.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on young stems, with darker vertical streaks; long ridges and furrows develop with age.

label: Leaves
text: Up to about two and a half inches, oblong, rounded at the base, very woolly when young and smooth and rather leathery when mature.

label: Flowers
text: Upright clusters of slightly fragrant white flowers with five narrow petals and up to twenty stamens, before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Small berry-like fruits, green turning red and finally dark purplish black in June.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on young trunks and branches, streaked with darker lines; long vertical splits and furrows open on old trunks.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, pointed and finely toothed, on slender stalks. Purplish-brown and silky beneath as they open, then light green.

label: Flowers
text: Inch-wide white to pale pink stars with long, narrow petals, six to fourteen in drooping clusters, before or with the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Small apple-like fruits, green turning red and then purple-black, from late spring into summer.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray, with pale horizontal lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to five inches long and nearly as wide, broadly oval with a rounded base and doubly toothed, often shallowly lobed edge; glossy and slightly hairy above.

label: Catkins
text: Purple-brown male catkins two to four inches long hang from the bare branches in March and April; the female catkins are only five-eighths of an inch.

label: Cones
text: Small woody cones, three-quarters by half an inch, that release winged seeds in fall and hang on through winter.

label: Bark
text: Light gray to greenish gray on young trees; gray to brownish gray on mature ones, in flat plates between shallow furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Up to five inches long, nearly round or widest toward the end, the tip blunt or notched, the edge wavy and toothed. Dark green and mostly smooth above.

label: Catkins
text: The male catkins form in fall and wait on the bare twigs all winter, then lengthen to three to six inches, reddish or brownish, in early spring.

label: Cones
text: Hard, woody, about three-quarters of an inch long. They release their seeds in fall and stay on the tree all winter and into the next summer.

label: Bark
text: Smooth, light brown to gray; young stems bright green, then light brown and covered with lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Nine to eighteen inches long and twice divided, into six to twelve pairs of side stalks, each with twenty to thirty pairs of tiny leaflets: feathery, like a fern.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant pink pompoms about an inch and a half long, of fifteen to twenty-five silky threads, from May to July.

label: Pods
text: Flat pods four to eight inches long and about an inch wide, green turning brown, each with five to ten oval seeds.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and pale gray, often with paler vertical stripes. Broken twigs smell foul.

label: Leaves
text: Eighteen to twenty-four inches long, with 10 to 41 smooth-edged leaflets. Look at the base of each: one or two notched teeth, each with a gland. Sumac's leaflets are toothed all along.

label: Flowers
text: Large clusters four to seven inches long of small yellow-green flowers in May and June, often with a foul smell.

label: Fruit
text: Large drooping clusters of flat, twisted, reddish-brown samaras, each with a seed in the middle.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown and smooth for years, then fissured into small rounded plates.

label: Leaves
text: Five to seven leaflets spread like fingers, four to eight inches long, dark green with a red midrib. They unfold covered in coppery hairs.

label: Flowers
text: Upright, cone-shaped spikes about eight inches tall of pink to red flowers with yellow throats, in mid-spring, visited by bees and hummingbirds.

label: Fruit
text: A prickly husk that splits to drop two or three glossy brown seeds. Poisonous.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and splotchy gray-brown at first, later with scaly patches.

label: Leaves
text: Five leaflets, sometimes seven, four to eight inches long, toothed and pointed, spread like fingers on a long stalk. Dark green above.

label: Flowers
text: Upright clusters six to ten inches tall of red to orange-red tubes an inch to an inch and a half long, in early spring.

label: Fruit
text: A smooth, light tan, leathery husk one to three inches across, holding one to three shiny brown seeds, each with a pale scar.

label: Bark
text: Corky and gray, furrowed on old trunks. Like the stems and flowers, it smells unpleasant when bruised.

label: Leaves
text: Five to seven smooth, finely toothed leaflets spread like a hand on a long stalk.

label: Flowers
text: Pale yellow-green flowers in upright clusters at the branch tips in May, their stamens sticking out past the four petals.

label: Fruit
text: A leathery husk covered in warts or prickles, holding one to three shiny brown seeds, each with the pale scar that makes the buck's eye.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light grayish brown, breaking with age into large, flat scales and plates.

label: Leaves
text: Nine to fifteen inches long, of five to seven sharply toothed, long-pointed leaflets four to six inches long, on a stalk as long as the leaflets.

label: Flowers
text: Upright clusters up to seven inches long of yellow four-petaled flowers, the stamens shorter than the petals, in April and May.

label: Fruit
text: A smooth, leathery, round to oval husk on a stout stalk, holding one to three dark brown buckeyes an inch and a half to two inches wide, ripe in late summer.

label: Bark
text: Thin and light brown, smooth on young stems and shallowly fissured with age.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, oval and mostly unlobed, with coarse, irregular teeth; young plants may show three to five shallow lobes. The leafstalk is tinged pink.

label: Flowers
text: Upright clusters two to three inches long of small greenish-white flowers in spring.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras with nearly parallel wings, three-quarters of an inch to an inch, turning red in summer.

label: Bark
text: Gray, flaking on mature trunks in small rectangular scales that show orange bark beneath.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches across, thick and leathery, with five coarsely toothed lobes, the lower two smaller, and a heart-shaped base. Hairy along the veins beneath. Little fall color.

label: Flowers
text: Hanging clusters four to five inches long of small yellow-green flowers in spring.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras about two inches across, ripening in fall; they spread on the wind and sprout readily wherever they land.

label: Shape
text: Wider than tall: eight to twelve feet high and up to fifteen across, spreading by suckers into a mounded colony. In early summer it is covered in upright white spikes.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, of five to seven leaflets three to eight inches long spread like fingers, gray-green and downy beneath. Golden yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Upright spikes six to twelve inches tall of half-inch white flowers in summer, their long stamens tipped with red anthers sticking out like bottlebrush bristles.

label: Fruit
text: Smooth, leathery, pear-shaped husks one to three inches long that split in late September and October around a polished brown seed with a pale scar.

label: Shape
text: Left unclipped, a dense, broadly rounded evergreen of many stems, sometimes growing into a small tree. Garden forms range from low mounds to narrow cones.

label: Leaves
text: Evergreen, half an inch to an inch and a half, glossy, oval and smooth-edged, in opposite pairs; light green beneath. They may turn orange-green in winter.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny creamy yellow flowers without petals, clustered where the leaves join the stem in spring. Fragrant.

label: Fruit
text: Round, third-inch capsules that ripen brown and split open, each part tipped with a little horn.

label: Shape
text: Dense, upright to rounded, six to twelve feet tall and as wide or wider, spreading by suckers.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, oval and smooth-edged, glossy dark green, rough to the touch, densely hairy beneath, and aromatic when bruised. Golden yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: About two inches across, brown to deep red, of many strap-like tepals, at the ends of short side shoots from mid-April into summer. Very fragrant.

label: Seed pods
text: Urn-shaped, wrinkled, leathery pods holding many seeds, soft green in August and fading to brown, often hanging on the bare twigs.

label: Shape
text: An open, rounded clump of many stems three to five feet tall and wide, growing wild on moist or rocky wooded slopes and streambanks.

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, broad, egg-shaped to round and sharply toothed, dark green above and pale beneath, in opposite pairs on gray-brown stems. Yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Flattened clusters two to eight inches across of tiny white fertile flowers, with a few larger sterile ones at the edge, from May to July and now and then into September.

label: Seed heads
text: The flower heads dry brown and hold small ribbed capsules that ripen from July to September.

label: Leaves
text: Large and leathery, three to eight inches long, with three to seven lobes like an oak's, fuzzy when young, in opposite pairs.

label: Flowers
text: Upright, cone-shaped clusters four to twelve inches long of creamy white flowers in late spring and summer. They fade to pink and then tan.

label: Dried flowers
text: The spent heads dry brown on the stems and hang on into winter, holding small seed capsules.

label: Fall color
text: One of the best of any shrub: the big lobed leaves turn wine red, orange and mahogany.

label: Leaves
text: Evergreen, glossy, dark green to blue-green, leathery, edged with four to eight flexible, forward-pointing spines on each side.

label: Flowers
text: Small white to pinkish-white flowers in spring, on separate male and female plants.

label: Berries
text: Bright red berries on purplish stems of female plants, from fall often until spring.

label: Leaves
text: One to four inches long, narrow, pointed and dark green, one at a time along arching stems.

label: Flowers
text: Arching spikes three to six inches long of tiny, lightly fragrant white flowers, opening from base to tip in May and June.

label: Seed capsules
text: The spikes become strings of slim, downy, third-inch woody capsules that hang on into the next year.

label: Fall color
text: Red, orange and gold, the leaves often hanging on into early winter.

label: Shape
text: A vigorous, upright to spreading shrub of many stems, semi-evergreen, holding some leaves into winter.

label: Leaves
text: About two and a half inches, oval to lance-shaped, smooth-edged and dark green, in opposite pairs.

label: Flowers
text: Small white tubular flowers with four lobes, in dense clusters at the shoot tips in June.

label: Berries
text: Small drupes, green ripening glossy black.

label: Shape
text: A large, rounded to spreading evergreen shrub of many stems. On the ridges of the southern Appalachians it grows wild in dense thickets.

label: Leaves
text: Evergreen, large and leathery, three to six inches long, broadly oval with a blunt tip and smooth edges, glossy dark green.

label: Flowers
text: Rounded clusters of fifteen to twenty lavender-pink funnels at the shoot tips in mid to late spring, the upper petal freckled green to yellow-brown.

label: Seed capsules
text: Dry, five-part capsules half an inch to an inch long at the shoot tips, ripening in fall.

label: Leaves
text: Three leaflets, glossy green to bluish green and coarsely round-toothed, the end one an inch and a half to three inches long and the side ones lopsided and smaller.

label: Flowers
text: Short spikes up to an inch long of tiny greenish-yellow flowers, on the bare stems in March and April for a week or two.

label: Fruit
text: Quarter-inch, hairy, red drupes in small clusters on female plants, from June into August.

label: Fall color
text: The three-part leaves turn orange, red or reddish purple in fall, often all on one plant.

label: Leaves
text: Compound, of five to eleven small toothed leaflets, half an inch to two inches long.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant, five-petaled, white to pale pink flowers half an inch to an inch across, in many-flowered clusters from late spring into early summer.

label: Hips
text: Quarter-inch red hips in clusters, ripening in late summer and hanging into fall, packed with seed.

label: Stipules
text: Look where each leaf stalk meets the stem: a pair of stipules with comb-like, fringed edges, which set it apart from other roses. The canes carry sturdy curved prickles.

label: Leaves
text: Five saw-toothed leaflets, each up to six inches long, spread like a hand. They open purplish, turn dull green, and color red to purple early in fall. Poison ivy has three.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-white flowers in branched clusters in the upper leaf axils, late spring into summer, mostly hidden by the leaves.

label: Berries
text: Blue-black berries up to three-eighths of an inch, on red stalks, hidden by the leaves until they fall.

label: Fall color
text: Red to purple, brightest in sun, the five-part leaves lighting up the trunks and walls it climbs.

label: Shape
text: A low, dense, rounded mound of upright stems, topped in early summer with flat pink flower clusters.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, sharply single- or double-toothed, lustrous dark green, downy on the veins beneath. On garden forms the young leaves are pink, red, purple, yellow or chartreuse.

label: Flowers
text: Flat-topped clusters up to eight inches across of tiny deep pink to rose-red flowers at the shoot tips in June and July, lightly fragrant.

label: Seed heads
text: The clusters dry into heads of small, brown, dry pods.

label: Bark
text: Smooth on the smaller stems, streaked lengthwise in white, black and pale gray; gray and rough on the larger ones. New shoots are smooth and red-brown.

label: Leaves
text: Of three finely toothed leaflets up to four inches long, each tapering to a short slender tip. Yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Nodding clusters of greenish-white bells, each a third of an inch long, hanging from the leaf axils in April and May.

label: Seed pods
text: Inflated, papery, three-lobed bladders one to two inches long, ripening in late summer and often hanging into early winter.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, oval and pointed, shallowly toothed, dark glossy green, set one at a time along the twig.

label: Flowers
text: Waxy white bells under an inch long, with yellow stamens, hanging on long stalks from short side shoots beneath the leaves. Slightly fragrant.

label: Fruit
text: Small, egg-shaped, gray-green to gray-white fruits hanging on long stalks, each with a single seed.

label: Shape
text: A small tree, vase-shaped when young, broadening with age into a rounded crown on low, horizontal branches. The leaves sit on top of the branches, the bells hang below them.

label: Shape
text: An upright, rounded clump of many arching stems, up to ten feet tall and wide, with good fall color.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long and nearly as wide, in opposite pairs, coarsely toothed, with straight, prominent veins running to the teeth.

label: Flowers
text: Flat-topped clusters up to four inches across of quarter-inch creamy flowers, each with five spreading petals and protruding yellow stamens.

label: Fruit
text: Quarter-inch blue-black berries from July to September, quickly eaten by birds.

label: Shape
text: Dense and arching, six to ten feet tall and wider still, the stems bowed under the flowers in late spring. Look at a new shoot: two lines of white hairs run down it.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, oval and pointed, finely toothed, downy on the veins beneath, on very short stalks. Some garden forms have purple or variegated leaves.

label: Flowers
text: Trumpets about an inch and a quarter long, pink, red or white, crowded along the stems in spring, with a few more later in summer.

label: Seed capsules
text: Small, oblong, two-part capsules that split open on the twig.

label: Bark
text: Shiny and bronze on young stems; on mature trees it peels in thin curls, coppery against the gray-brown beneath.

label: Leaves
text: Three to eight inches long, of seven to thirteen oval leaflets, dark olive green, with no fall color to speak of.

label: Flowers
text: Upright spikes four to six inches long of fragrant white pea flowers, in late spring and early summer.

label: Pods
text: Flat seed pods two to three inches long, ripening brown after the flowers.

label: Leaves
text: Enormous, up to three feet long and a foot wide, smooth green above and silvery white and downy beneath, clustered toward the branch tips.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant creamy-white cups eight to fourteen inches across, with six to nine tepals, the inner ones purple at the base, in May and June.

label: Fruit
text: Oval, hairy, cone-like fruits two to three inches long, green turning red in late summer, opening to let red seeds hang out on threads.

label: Winter bud
text: A large bud, silvery with silky hairs, tips the stout twig in winter. Below it sits a big leaf scar, and a stipule scar circles the stem.
source: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Up to two feet long and ten inches wide, crowded at the ends of the stems around a pale green bud shaped like a paintbrush.

label: Flowers
text: Bowl-shaped, creamy white, six to ten inches across, with six to twelve tepals, in April and May. They smell unpleasant.

label: Fruit
text: Upright, cone-like and pink, about four inches long, from July into October.

label: Umbrella
text: Seen from above, the big leaves, ten to twenty-four inches long, radiate in whorl-like clusters from the ends of the stems, like the spokes of an umbrella. Often grows with several stems.

label: Leaves
text: Three glossy, dark green leaflets two and a half to four inches long, smooth-edged or slightly toothed, on a stalk two to six inches long. Crushed, they smell unpleasant.

label: Flowers
text: Quarter-inch, greenish-white to greenish-yellow flowers with four or five petals, in clusters, with an unpleasant scent. Most plants are male or female.

label: Fruit
text: Round, papery wafers about an inch across, a seed or two at the center and a net-veined wing all around, hanging in hop-like clusters.

label: Leaves
text: Three to eight inches long, opposite, leathery and lustrous bright green, downy and whitish beneath. Young leaves are toothed, mature ones smooth-edged.

label: Flowers
text: Snow-white, fragrant, fringe-like flowers in four-inch clusters at the ends of the shoots in spring.

label: Fruit
text: Half-inch, dark blue, olive-like fruits on female trees.

label: Shape
text: A small tree or large shrub, often with several trunks, upright when young and rounding out with age.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, with three lobes, the middle one long and pointed, and doubly toothed edges.

label: Flowers
text: Small, fragrant, creamy flowers in loose clusters in spring as the leaves open.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras up to an inch long, turning red in summer and into fall.

label: Fall color
text: Red to orange, sometimes yellow, the leaves on distinctly red stalks.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown with smooth streaks on young trees; later darker, with irregular broad ridges and narrow furrows, especially near the base, often spotted gray.

label: Leaves
text: Three to seven inches long, lustrous dark green, with seven bristle-tipped lobes and deep, C-shaped gaps between them. Scarlet late in fall.

label: Acorns
text: Half an inch to an inch long, alone or in pairs, half covered by a deep, bowl-like cap of shiny scales. The bare end often shows fine concentric rings.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray-brown on young trees; dark brown on mature ones, with deep furrows between flat ridges.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long and an inch or so wide, smooth-edged, leathery, shiny dark green, paler beneath. They drop in spring as the new leaves open.

label: Acorns
text: Half an inch long, dark brown and stalkless, up to a third covered by a gray, scaly cup. They take two years to ripen.

label: Bark
text: Gray, with deep furrows between scaly ridges or plates.

label: Leaves
text: Six to eight inches long, narrow at the base and broad toward the tip, with five to nine deep, rounded lobes. Shiny dark green above, gray-green and hairy beneath.

label: Acorns
text: Half an inch to an inch long, one or two to a stalk, almost wholly enclosed in a cup of gray, downy scales. Trees bear from about twenty-five.

label: Bark
text: Thick and dark reddish brown, cut into deep furrows between broad, rounded ridges.

label: Leaves
text: Four to eight inches long, oval and pointed, edged with coarse rounded teeth or shallow lobes. Gray-green and hairy beneath. Reddish yellow in fall.

label: Acorns
text: An inch to an inch and a half long, alone or in pairs, nearly stalkless, a third covered by a thin, reddish-brown cup of fused scales.

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers hang in yellow-green catkins in April; the female flowers are separate, on short stalks.

label: Bark
text: Thick, smooth and grayish, becoming furrowed and darker gray.

label: Leaves
text: Up to seven inches long, with two to four pairs of pointed, bristle-tipped lobes and gaps cut half to three-quarters of the way to the midrib. Shiny dark green above, pale beneath.

label: Acorns
text: Oblong, three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a quarter, alone or in pairs, less than a third covered by a shallow, scaly, bowl-shaped cap.

label: Bark
text: Thin, light ashy gray, rough and irregularly fissured into flaky plates.

label: Leaves
text: Four to eight inches long, shiny and smooth above, dull and sometimes white-hairy beneath, edged with regular, sharp-pointed teeth like a chestnut's.

label: Catkins
text: Drooping yellow-green male catkins with the new leaves; the female flowers sit on short stems in the leaf axils.

label: Acorns
text: Oval, light brown, half an inch to an inch long, one or two together, a quarter to half covered by a thin, gray, downy cup. They ripen in one season, every year.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on young trees; brown with age, with reddish layers showing in the furrows between hard, flat ridges.

label: Needles
text: Flat and glossy dark green, an inch to an inch and a third long, slightly notched at the tip, with two green-white bands beneath. They lie in two flat rows either side of the shoot.

label: Cones
text: Upright, an inch and a third to four inches long, the bracts hidden between the scales. About six months after they form they break apart, releasing winged seeds.

label: Shape
text: A narrow, conical spire, often irregular at the top with age. The coastal form is one of the tallest firs in the world.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown, peeling in long strips on mature trees.

label: Foliage
text: Short, blunt scale leaves pressed close in flattened fans, of two sizes. Turn a spray over: whitish X- or Y-shaped marks line the underside.

label: Cones
text: Small and round, about half an inch, of eight to ten scales, green ripening orange-brown.

label: Shape
text: Broadly pyramidal and spreading, 50 to 75 feet tall in time but only 10 to 25 wide.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown and fairly smooth, peeling in strips.

label: Foliage
text: Small, pointed scale leaves in flat, horizontal sprays, bright green with a silvery line beneath. Hinoki's are blunt.

label: Cones
text: Small and round, green when young and turning brown.

label: Shape
text: Pyramidal when young, growing loose and open with age; in gardens usually 20 to 30 feet tall, larger in the wild.

label: Bark
text: Light reddish brown and fibrous, in flat, crossing ridges that sometimes spiral up the trunk; it peels easily in strips.

label: Foliage
text: Soft green to blue-green scale leaves, each with a conspicuous resin gland, in irregular, overlapping, flattened sprays.

label: Cones
text: A quarter inch across, in clusters, purple when young and ripening brown, with a crumpled look.

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny red-yellow pollen cones sit at the ends of the shoots in spring, apart from the small green seed cones.

label: Shape
text: Narrow and pyramidal when young, rounding with age, thirty to forty feet tall. Planted forms range from slim blue columns to low mounds.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown or gray, shedding in thin, fibrous strips.

label: Foliage
text: Scale leaves in opposite pairs, bluish silver to light or dark green, usually with an inconspicuous gland on each.

label: Cones
text: Round, berry-like, a fifth to a third of an inch, green and frosted at first, ripening dark blue under a heavy white bloom.

label: Bark
text: Pinkish gray and smooth when young; gray and flaking in thin, rounded plates as the tree matures.

label: Needles
text: A quarter to half an inch long, shorter than most spruces', glossy dark green, four-sided and blunt, packed densely all around the shoot.

label: Cones
text: Slender and pointed, hanging, ripening brown.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small red pollen cones, under an inch long, crowd the shoots in late April and early May, mostly on the lower part of the tree.

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown on the surface, reddish brown beneath, in thin, irregular, flaky patches.

label: Needles
text: Half an inch or so long, four-sided, sharp, shiny dark yellow-green, tending to point forward along the shoot.

label: Cones
text: Oval, an inch to an inch and a half long, purplish green when young and ripening brown.

label: Shape
text: A tall, slender spruce, 70 to 100 feet high but only 30 to 40 wide, with a narrow, conical crown.

label: Needles
text: Short and slightly twisted, five to a bundle, with white lines that give them a blue-green, silvery look.

label: Cones
text: Small and egg-shaped, reddish brown.

label: Shape
text: Dense and pyramidal when young; with age wide-spreading, flat-topped and picturesque, its needles tufted on tiered branches.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray at first, breaking into scales that darken with age.

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown to grayish black, becoming rougher and irregularly furrowed with age.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches, round in outline with three to five lobes, thick and leathery, the sides drooping as if wilted. Red, orange and yellow in fall.

label: Fruit
text: Clusters of paired samaras up to an inch long, ripening in late summer.

label: Flowers
text: Yellow-green flowers hang in drooping clusters two to four inches long, each on a thread-thin stalk; the female clusters are shorter.

label: Bark
text: Ashy light brown, peeling in long, loose strips to show cinnamon orange-brown beneath, even on young trees.

label: Leaves
text: Three leaflets about three inches long, dark green and a little fuzzy, irregularly toothed. One of the most reliable trees for fall color: orange, scarlet, purple and gold in October.

label: Flowers
text: Pink to greenish-yellow flowers in clusters of three in April, which gives the tree its name.

label: Bark
text: Often purple-tinged when young; older branches gray-brown, and mature trunks rough and fissured.

label: Flowers
text: Clusters of greenish-yellow flowers in April and May as the leaves open.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches, with five smooth-edged lobes; the two at the base carry small spurs pointing back toward the stalk, which bleeds milky sap when broken. Yellow, orange and red in fall.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras up to an inch and a half long, the wings spread at about a right angle.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray with shallow interlacing ridges at first; later in long, loose plates that give it a shaggy look.

label: Leaves
text: Large, of five to nine, usually seven, finely toothed, lance-shaped leaflets four to eight inches long.

label: Nuts
text: A thick husk, green turning brown, that splits into four around an egg-shaped tan nut, ripe in fall.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and polished, brown to cinnamon, peeling to leave patches of cream and gray.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, sharply toothed, lustrous dark green, clustered at the ends of the branches.

label: Flowers
text: Spikes four to six inches long of many fragrant white flowers, held out horizontally from the branch tips, from July into late August.

label: Fall color
text: The leaves, crowded at the branch tips, turn bronze-red to maroon.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, furrowed and ridged, breaking into flaky, scaly plates with age.

label: Leaves
text: Blue-green, smooth-edged, widest above the middle, wedge-shaped at the base and slightly notched at the tip.

label: Smoke
text: The flowers are tiny, but their branched stalks, six to ten inches long, grow long red or purple hairs that make a smoky haze, best on male plants.

label: Fall color
text: Some of the best fall color of any native tree or shrub: the rounded leaves turn red and orange.

label: Stems
text: Grayish brown, irregularly furrowed and shredding on older stems.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, oval and toothed, in pairs or sometimes threes, dark green above and light green beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Cone-shaped clusters six to eight inches long of creamy white flowers in summer, on the new growth.

label: Late flowers
text: The white flower clusters do not drop when they finish: they turn pinkish rose as autumn nears, then tan to brown, as they dry.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown to gray, rough, covered in irregular lengthwise scales; with age it becomes fissured and scaly.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three inches long, yellowish green, toothed and sometimes lobed.

label: Flowers
text: Four to six fragrant blossoms together, an inch to an inch and three-quarters across, pink in bud and opening white to pale pink, for about two weeks in May.

label: Fruit
text: Round, smooth and waxy, three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a half across, green ripening yellowish green, fragrant and sour.

label: Bark
text: On mature trees it flakes away in patches of green, white and tan.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to four and a half inches long, oval, the edge coarsely toothed and wavy above the middle.

label: Flowers
text: Half an inch across, without petals: tufts of five to fifteen red stamens among brown bracts, on the bare twigs in late winter and early spring.

label: Fall color
text: Yellow, orange and burgundy, often on the same branch.

label: Needles
text: In pairs, one to three inches long, stiff, thick and blunt, dark green, crowded along the shoots.

label: Young cones
text: Small seed cones, red when young, sit at the tips of the new shoots; the greenish-yellow pollen cones are a quarter inch long.

label: Cones
text: An inch to two and a half inches long, stalkless, rounded and brown.

label: Shape
text: Usually a low, broad, bushy shrub of many stems, wider than tall; sometimes a small tree up to 25 feet. Garden forms are often only two to five feet high.

label: Bark
text: Flaking away in irregular patches to show a mottle of brown, tan, gray, olive and cinnamon.

label: Leaves
text: Small, an inch to two and a half inches long, glossy dark green and toothed, only slightly lopsided at the base.

label: Fruit
text: Flat, papery samaras about half an inch long, light brown, appearing in fall and hanging into early winter.

label: Bark
text: Thick, fibrous and reddish brown, hard, furrowed between scaly ridges; cinnamon brown beneath. The trunk flares into buttresses at the base.

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny round pollen cones, an eighth of an inch or so, one at each shoot tip among the scale leaves, shedding in winter.

label: Cones
text: Hard, reddish brown, egg-shaped, half an inch to an inch long, ripening in their first year.

label: Shape
text: Pyramidal with horizontal branches when young; with age it grows more narrowly conical and sheds its lower branches, leaving a long, clean, columnar trunk.

label: Shape
text: Two forms on one plant: young growth trails along the ground as a dense evergreen mat or climbs, while older, mature growth becomes a sprawling shrub.

label: Leaves
text: Evergreen, glossy, dark green or variegated, on stems that climb walls and trunks by little rootlets.

label: Flowers
text: Quarter-inch, greenish-white, four-petaled flowers on stalks from the axils of mature leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Round, pale, quarter-inch capsules that split in fall to show seeds in fleshy orange coats.

label: Leaves
text: Three to four inches long, oblong to oval, sharply toothed, pale green beneath. Yellow to red in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Inch-wide, five-petaled white flowers, two to five together, fragrant, crowding the bare branches in March and April before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Round plums about an inch across, thick-skinned, red to purple over bright yellow flesh, ripening in July and August.

label: Thorny twigs
text: Dark reddish-brown twigs, often contorted, with short, stout side branchlets that end in a sharp point like a thorn. Left alone, the suckers form thickets armed with them.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three inches long, oval, finely toothed and shiny, pale beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant five-petaled flowers, white on the species, with twenty to thirty stamens, single or two or three together, crowded along the twigs.

label: Fruit
text: Smooth, round plums up to an inch and a quarter across, yellow or red, ripening mid to late summer. Few form in cool years.

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long and narrow, with a long point, fine teeth, and two small glands at the base of the blade.

label: Flowers
text: Pink, five-petaled, an inch to an inch and a half across, single or in pairs, before the leaves in spring. Lightly fragrant.

label: Fruit
text: Peaches: fuzzy, juicy, yellow to orange flushed red when ripe in summer, around a large, rough stone.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, oval with a long point, edged with fine teeth tipped with bristles. Two to four small glands sit on the stalk.

label: Flowers
text: Clusters of three to five flowers an inch and a half across, on stalks up to an inch and a half long, from late March into April; usually double on garden forms.

label: Fruit
text: Small, round, black cherries in late summer, when there are any; the double forms seldom fruit.

label: Shape
text: Fifteen to twenty-five feet tall and as wide; spreading, vase-shaped or weeping, depending on the variety.

label: Leaves
text: One to two inches long, oval and toothed, reddish purple all season.

label: Stems
text: Smooth and dark reddish brown on young stems; gray to gray-brown and fissured on old ones.

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch, fragrant, pinkish-white flowers with red calyxes, in mid-spring after the leaves.

label: Leaves
text: Oval with a long point, bright green, each tooth tipped with a tiny gland, hairy on the veins beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Pale pink to snow-white, five or six together in tight clusters, with a slight almond scent, lasting two to three weeks.

label: Shape
text: Fast-growing, open and spreading, a broad vase or rounded crown on arching branches.

label: Bark
text: Smooth, glossy gray-brown, banded with prominent horizontal lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Narrow, ribbed, grass-like leaves ten to thirty inches long and seldom an inch wide, arching from the base in a clump, shorter than the flower stems.

label: Flowers
text: Three large, drooping outer sepals and three upright inner petals, blue-violet veined with white on the species; garden forms come in white, yellow, wine and purple.

label: Seed pods
text: Dry seed pods on top of the stalks, turning brown and splitting open at the top.

label: Shape
text: An upright, arching clump about two feet tall; a mature clump can hold twelve to twenty flowers at once, on stems above the leaves.

label: Leaves
text: Huge, bright green, paddle-shaped, up to six feet long and two wide, unfurling from the top of a stem made of rolled leaf bases.

label: Flowers
text: A hanging, torpedo-shaped bud at the top of the stem in summer, its reddish-brown to purple bracts opening on rows of yellow-orange flowers.

label: Fruit
text: Short green or yellow bananas, two to four inches long, inedible: thin white pulp packed with black seeds.

label: Shape
text: Not a trunk but a false stem of tightly overlapping leaf bases. Each one dies after it fruits, and new shoots from the roots replace it, so the plant grows as a spreading clump.

label: Bark
text: Ridged and furrowed, cracking into angular plates that flake to leave yellowish patches.

label: Needles
text: In pairs, about three inches long, stiff, glossy dark green and prickly.

label: Cones
text: One to three inches long, single or in twos or threes, purple-blue when young.

label: Shape
text: Conical when young, its branches in whorls curving upward; with age it becomes oval and dense. A slow grower.

label: Needles
text: In pairs, five to six and a half inches long, dark glossy green, crowded densely on the shoots so each year's growth runs into the last. They fall in their fourth year, leaving the twigs rough with little pegs.

label: Cones
text: Egg-shaped, about two inches long, shiny pale brown and almost stalkless, with no prickles on the scales.

label: Bark
text: Furrowed and cross-checked into irregular, rectangular, scaly plates, up to two inches thick on old trees: thick enough to carry it through most surface fires.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny, short-lived pollen cones crowd the base of each new shoot, mostly in the lower crown; the seed cones form higher up, on separate branches, which keeps the tree from pollinating itself.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Bark
text: Dark gray-brown, dotted with pale lenticels. Scratched, it gives off a strong, rather acrid smell.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, oval and pointed, finely toothed, dull dark green, with two or more small glands on the stalk.

label: Flowers
text: Fragrant white flowers a third to half an inch wide, in drooping or spreading spikes three to six inches long at the ends of short leafy shoots.

label: Fruit
text: Round black cherries a quarter to a third of an inch across, harsh and bitter.

label: Bark
text: Smooth, lustrous, brownish yellow to copper, peeling in horizontal curls like a birch's.

label: Leaves
text: Three or four inches long, oval and pointed, very finely toothed, hairy on the veins. Turn one over: the underside is covered with tiny glandular dots.

label: Flowers
text: Small white flowers, the stamens longer than the petals, in downy spikes two to three inches long on last year's wood.

label: Fruit
text: Tiny cherries, about a quarter inch across, red at first and black by late summer.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to five inches, round to oval, edged with large, broad teeth: quaking aspen's are fine. Gray-woolly when they open, soon dark green, on a slender stalk flattened toward the top.

label: Catkins
text: Fuzzy catkins an inch and a half to two and a half inches long, on the bare twigs before the leaves, from winter buds coated with fine down.

label: Seed
text: The female catkins double in length as they ripen into strings of small green capsules that split to release cottony seed.

label: Bark
text: Smooth on young trees; after three decades or more it roughens and develops grooves.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Bark
text: Gray on young trees, soon reddish or yellowish brown and scaly, then gray again, flaking off in thin plates.

label: Needles
text: Soft, in tufts on short spur shoots and singly along the new long shoots. They begin to yellow in September and color fully by early October before falling.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Cones
text: Small, oblong, half to three-quarters of an inch long, brown when ripe, opening on the twig among the needle tufts.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Pollen cones
text: Small and solitary, opening with the new needles: the male cones yellow and round, mostly on one- and two-year-old twigs; the young seed cones reddish, mostly on older ones.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Bark and spines
text: Gray-brown with pale lenticels. Young branches are slightly winged, and the stipules at each joint harden into a pair of stiff spines about a quarter inch long.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three inches long, of four to six pairs of small oval leaflets, with no leaflet at the tip: the stalk ends in a bristle-like spine.

label: Flowers
text: Yellow pea flowers five-eighths to seven-eighths of an inch long, one to a thin downy stalk, several together from scaly buds on last year's wood.

label: Pods
text: Slender pods an inch and a half to two inches long.

label: Leaves
text: Five to eight inches long, oblong, rounded or heart-shaped at the base, edged with triangular, bristle-tipped teeth. Often felted whitish beneath, though downiness varies even on one tree.

label: Catkins
text: Cream male catkins four to five inches long, upright and arching from the shoot tips.

label: Burs
text: A husk about two inches wide, covered in straw-colored spines and soft down, usually holding two or three nuts.

label: Trunks and shoots
text: Often branches low, and can grow almost shrubby. The young shoots are hairy, some thinly with long hairs, others with a short velvety down.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark and shoots
text: Pale, smooth and gray on young stems. The young shoots are so flexible they can be bent double without breaking.

label: Needles
text: Five to a bundle, two and a half to three and a half inches long, three-sided with white lines on all sides, often pointing forward along the shoot. They stay about seven years.

label: Cones
text: Three to five inches long and an inch and a half thick before they open, with thick scales.

label: Pollen cones
text: Just over half an inch long, short and broad, pale red or yellow, in clusters. The seed cones, by contrast, sit singly or in twos and threes.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, with irregular knobbly ridges after about thirty years. The trunk sprouts thickets of shoots and burrs, especially at its base.

label: Leaves
text: Three to four inches, nearly round with a lopsided heart-shaped base, matte green above and paler beneath, with large tufts of pale brown hair in the main vein angles underneath.

label: Flowers
text: Drooping clusters, usually of seven pale yellow flowers, hanging from a leafy bract.

label: Fruit
text: Round nutlets about a third of an inch across, densely covered in brown hairs, under the bract.

label: Leaves
text: Shaped like the species', broad and five-lobed with a few long points, but deep purple from spring to fall, with little fall color. Among the best of the purple-leaved selections.

label: Pods
text: Smooth, flat, purple-brown pods two to four inches long, each with four to eight kidney-shaped seeds. They ripen from July and often hang on through the winter.

label: Fronds
text: Airy, blue-green fans of small, lobed leaflets shaped like shells or half-moons, thin and a little waxy beneath. Light brown spores show along the outer edges of the leaflets.

label: Shape
text: One to three feet tall, arching and airy, spreading slowly on creeping, branching rhizomes into large colonies. In spring the coiled fiddleheads come up pink.

label: Fronds
text: Eight to twenty-five inches long and only about four wide, soft and yellow-green, of about twenty pairs of divided leaflets that shrink steadily toward both ends.

label: Fronds
text: Up to three feet long, elliptical and finely cut, three times divided, rising in a clump from one point. The lowest leaflets are shorter than the middle ones. Brown-covered spore cases line the undersides.

label: Shape
text: An arching clump of fronds from a single crown, spreading slowly, into a loose ground cover.

label: Fronds
text: Plume-like, broadest above the middle and narrowing steadily to the base, with thirty to fifty pairs of lobed leaflets; the tip ends abruptly. In summer short, stiff, lyre-shaped spore fronds rise in the center and turn brown and woody.

label: Fiddleheads
text: In spring the new fronds rise from the center of each clump as tightly coiled fiddleheads, then unroll into the vase-shaped ring of plumes. Underground runners start new clumps nearby.

label: Fronds
text: Leathery, lance-shaped and evergreen. Each leaflet has a small lobe at its base, like the toe of a stocking. Spores form only on the last third of the fertile fronds. In spring the fiddleheads are silvery and scaly.

label: Flowers
text: Inch-long to two-inch white bottlebrushes with a sweet honey scent, at the branch tips in April and May, before the leaves.

label: Leaves
text: One to two and a half inches, oval and leathery, blue-green to dark green, hairy, with a quilted surface, toothed only on the upper half. The buds are very hairy.

label: Fall color
text: Orange, yellow and scarlet.

label: Flowers
text: White bottlebrush spikes one to three inches long in April and May, made not of petals but of twelve to thirty-two white stamens; some smell of honey.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long and nearly as wide, leathery, blue-green above and grayish to whitish beneath, coarsely toothed on the upper half.

label: Fall color
text: Red, orange and yellow, often all on one leaf.

label: Flowers
text: Bright yellow, about two inches across, usually of five petals, at the ends of short leafy shoots on last year's stems in April and May.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to four inches long, narrow, long-pointed, sharply double-toothed and pleated along the veins; bright green above, paler beneath. Some turn yellow in fall.

label: Shape
text: Upright, arching, slender green stems that make a broad, dense, twiggy mass up to seven feet tall and nine wide. The stems stay bright green all winter.

label: Flowers
text: Rosy purple pea flowers half to three-quarters of an inch, five to eight together in tight clusters straight from old stems and even the trunk, for two to three weeks in early spring.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches, broadly heart-shaped, smooth-edged, leathery and lustrous dark green, with five veins fanning from the base.

label: Needles
text: Flat and pointed, olive to dark green above and lighter beneath. The shoots stay green for two years before turning brown.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small round pollen cones beneath the shoots of male plants.

label: Fruit
text: On female plants, a single seed sits in a showy red, fleshy cup.

label: Bark
text: Ridged and fissured, peeling in thin, fibrous strips.

label: Foliage
text: Two kinds, often on one plant: flat, dark green scale leaves on mature shoots, and sharp, bluish-green needles on young ones.

label: Cones
text: Fleshy, berry-like, blue cones on female plants; the male pollen cones are brown and fall apart when spent.

label: Foliage
text: Mature leaves are tiny scales pressed to the stem in four rows; young ones are awl-like, in pairs. New growth is yellow-green.

label: Cones
text: Blue, berry-like cones under half an inch, with two or three seeds, on short curved stalks. They ripen in their second year.

label: Winter color
text: A low, spreading mat whose green to blue-green summer foliage often takes on a purplish tinge in winter.

label: Needles
text: Stiff, under an inch and a half, in tufts of ten to thirty on short spur shoots, curving toward the tip. Color varies from bright green to silvery blue.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray and fissured, breaking into small scaly plates, and fragrant.

label: Needles
text: Three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a half, stiff, dark green to almost black-green with silvery blue lines, thirty to forty in a tuft on each spur shoot.

label: Cones
text: Upright, barrel-shaped, three to five inches long, purple-brown, with a flat or slightly sunken top. They break apart on the branch, shedding seed from ripening until spring.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, ridged and furrowed.

label: Leaves
text: Three to eight inches long, glossy, oval with a long point and a toothed edge, like an elm's; mature leaves look slightly wrinkled. The twigs have no bud at their tips.

label: Bark
text: Dark red-brown to silvery brown, fibrous, in many thin vertical ridges.

label: Foliage
text: Tiny, rounded, overlapping leaves up to a third of an inch, with a blue-gray bloom, on slender shoots that stand straight up from the branches.

label: Fall color
text: A deciduous conifer: in fall the upright shoots turn bright orange to rusty brown.

label: Shape
text: An open, pyramidal tree, slow to grow: about 35 feet after twenty years, though old trees reach 70. A large taproot anchors it, even in standing water.

label: Leaves
text: Glossy and broad, four to eight inches across, usually with three pointed, coarsely toothed lobes and a heart-shaped base. Young shoots carry smaller leaves of three separate leaflets, tinged bronze.

label: Berries
text: Dull, dark bluish-black berries up to a third of an inch, hidden under the leaves until they drop in fall.

label: Fall color
text: Green turning to burgundy and red in a spectacular show; once they fall, the berries they hid come into view.

label: Catkins
text: Silvery-green to yellow catkins in April and May, on separate male and female trees; the male ones, one to two inches long, are the showier.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long and only half to three-quarters of an inch wide, finely toothed and long-pointed, light green above and grayish beneath. The twigs are reddish to yellowish brown and smooth.

label: Flowers
text: Six to twelve fragrant, pale yellow to cream flowers hang in each cluster from a long, strap-like bract.

label: Leaves
text: Small for a linden, two to three inches long and wide, with three to five pointed, toothed lobes, almost like a maple's. Dark green above, paler beneath; a mild yellow in fall.

label: Needles
text: About an inch long, flat, shiny dark green, with a rounded or notched tip; the undersides are silvery white.

label: Cones
text: Upright, purple-brown, about two and a half inches long, with yellow-green bracts whose tips poke out and curl down between the scales. When ripe the scales fall with the seeds, leaving bare spikes on the branch.

label: Bark
text: Flaky from a young age, gray to silvery gray; on old trees gray-brown, scaly and rough.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Needles
text: Half to three-quarters of an inch long and four-sided, crowding forward and upward along the shoot. Each lasts three or four years.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Cones
text: The smallest cones of any spruce, with thin scales rounded and smooth at the edge. They ripen in August or September.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Pollen cones
text: Dense pollen cones about half an inch long. The seed cones ripen two or three months after the pollen is shed.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Flowers
text: Pink buds open to fragrant white flowers about an inch across, covering the shrub in spring, often heavily only every other year.

label: Fruit
text: Half-inch crabapples, yellow to red, ripening in fall and lasting long on the branches.

label: Leaves
text: Dark green, some with side lobes, turning yellow in fall against the red fruit. The young branches are purple and finely hairy.

label: Bark
text: Shiny gray-brown and scaly, but thin: a knock from a mower or trimmer wounds it easily.
source: University of Connecticut Plant Database; University of Florida

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, peeling in long strips to show lighter bark beneath, most striking in winter.

label: Fruit
text: After the white flowers fall, the cherry-red to rose-purple calyx stays around each small fruit, making a second show in fall.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, three to six inches long, smooth-edged and leathery, with three conspicuous veins running from the base, on short reddish stalks.

label: Flowers
text: Small, fragrant white flowers in many little clusters making up loose sprays at the shoot tips.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown, thick, spongy and fibrous, deeply furrowed.

label: Foliage
text: Bluish-green leaves an eighth to half an inch long, awl-shaped and three-sided, pointing forward along the twig. Older twigs shed them and turn reddish brown and scaly.

label: Cones
text: Oval and woody, about two inches long, green to reddish brown. They reach full size by August of their first year.

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny round pollen cones, a fifth of an inch or so, one at the tip of each shoot, on the same branches as the seed cones.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, usually three-lobed with triangular, smooth-edged lobes and three main veins from the base; glossy green above and whitish beneath. Fall color yellow, orange, red or purple.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras an inch or a little more long, the wings spread at various angles, ripening from August to October.

label: Bark
text: Gray and slightly corky, developing lengthwise fissures with age and becoming scaly.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches across, usually five-lobed with narrow gaps and a few blunt teeth, downy beneath, on a long stalk that bleeds milky sap when snapped. Yellow in fall.

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches across, thin, cut halfway or more into nine to eleven sharply double-toothed lobes; dark green above and densely white-downy beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small flowers in clusters at the shoot tips, the sepals reddish purple and the petals white to cream.

label: Fall color
text: Plant hunters such as E. H. Wilson called it a brilliant autumn sight in its native forests, in yellow, orange and red. Some garden trees disappoint, holding dull brown leaves on the twigs before they drop.

label: Bark
text: Silvery gray and smooth on young trees, as both parents' bark is; the plates come later.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Usually five-lobed, closer to a silver maple's, but the middle lobe is seldom cut into lobes of its own as a silver maple's usually is. Fall color runs from red to yellow.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras an inch and a quarter to two and a half inches long, the wings finely lined. Some named forms, such as 'Marmo', are male trees and set no seed at all.

label: Bark
text: Grayish white to ashen white, tight to the trunk, never peeling or even flaking; paper birch's peels.

label: Leaves
text: One to four inches long, triangular with a long, drawn-out tip, shallowly double-toothed, smooth on both sides.

label: Catkins
text: Yellow male catkins hang from the thin gray twigs in spring; the female catkins stand upright on the shoots.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Seed catkins
text: The female catkins become drooping, stalked, cone-like clusters of many small winged nutlets, which the wind carries far. Trees seed heavily every year from about age eight.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Leaves
text: Half an inch to two and a quarter inches long, widest toward the tip, with three or five shallow rounded or pointed lobes, toothed, dark glossy green.

label: Flowers
text: White, five-eighths of an inch across, six to twelve together in May, with red anthers and two or three styles in each flower.

label: Fruit
text: Red, roundish haws a quarter to three-quarters of an inch long, each with two or three stones. Thorns about an inch long arm the twigs.

label: Bark
text: Shreddy or scaly on young stems. Older trunks are weakly furrowed and often fluted or knotted, until the trunk looks like a twisted bundle of thin stems.

label: Leaves
text: Ten to twelve inches long, compound, of toothed leaflets. Buff-yellow in late summer, deep yellow in fall. In winter, look for the black buds.

label: Flowers
text: Short, dense clusters of tiny flowers from the joints of last year's twigs in April, before the leaves.

label: Trunk
text: The trunk of one of Europe's largest broadleaf trees, up to 140 feet in the best sites. The bark is pale and fissured; the young twigs are smooth and gray.

label: Keys
text: Winged seeds about an inch and a half long, hanging in large bunches; trees bear them in great numbers. The tip of the wing may be blunt, notched or pointed.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Large, upright goblets of nine tepals on the bare branches in spring, white inside and stained pink to purple at the base outside; color and size vary between the many cultivars.

label: Leaves
text: Up to eight inches long, broadly oval to widest above the middle, glossy dark green above and paler beneath, with fine hairs along the midrib and main veins.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray, often marked by sapsuckers with neat horizontal rows of small holes. Large, hairy flower buds sit at the twig tips a year ahead of bloom.

label: Fruit
